title.en: Volume 118 Biographies 43: Zhang, Wei, Han, Song, Xi, Two Li's, Pei

sentences.zh: 張廷珪，河南濟源人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui was a man of Jiyuan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui was from Jiyuan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 慷慨有志尚。

translations.literal: He was generous and possessed lofty aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補白水尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi degree, he was made assistant magistrate of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 舉制科異等。

translations.literal: He was recommended for the special examination category and placed in the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for a special examination and ranked in the top class.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史，按劾平直。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor, and his impeachments were fair and impartial.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to investigating censor, where his investigations were even-handed.

sentences.zh: 武后稅天下浮屠錢，營佛祠於白司馬阪，作大象，廷珪諫，以爲：「傾四海之財，殫萬民之力，窮山之木爲塔，極冶之金爲象，然猶有爲之法，不足高也。

translations.literal: Empress Wu levied money from Buddhist monks throughout the realm, built a Buddhist shrine at White Sima Slope, and cast a great elephant; Tinggui remonstrated, saying: "To drain the wealth of the four seas and exhaust the strength of the myriad people, to use up mountain timber for pagodas and the utmost smelted metal for images—yet these are still methods that depend on action and are not lofty enough.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu taxed Buddhist clergy empire-wide to build a temple at White Sima Slope and cast a colossal elephant, Tinggui protested: "You are pouring the wealth of the empire and the labor of the people into pagodas of mountain timber and images of refined metal—yet even these are merely contrived works and not truly sublime.

sentences.zh: 填塞澗穴，覆壓蟲蟻，且巨億計。

translations.literal: Ravines and caves are filled in, insects and ants are crushed beneath, and the cost runs to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Gullies are choked, countless small creatures are buried, and the expense runs into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 工員窮窶，驅役爲勞，饑渴所致，疾疹方作。

translations.literal: Laborers are destitute; driven to service they grow weary; hunger and thirst bring on sickness and fever.
translations.idiomatic: Workers are impoverished, worn down by forced labor; hunger and thirst spread disease among them.

sentences.zh: 又僧尼乞丐自贍，而州縣督輸，星火迫切，鬻賣以充，非浮屠所謂隨喜者。

translations.literal: Moreover monks and nuns beg to support themselves, yet prefectures and counties press for delivery with urgent haste like sparks flying; they sell possessions to meet quotas—this is not what Buddhism calls voluntary offering.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns already live by alms, yet local officials demand payments with frantic urgency, forcing them to sell what little they have—hardly the voluntary devotion Buddhism teaches.

sentences.zh: 今天下虛竭，蒼生雕弊，謂宜先邊境，實府庫，養人力。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is drained empty and the common people are worn to ruin; I say we should first secure the borders, fill the treasuries, and nurture human strength."
translations.idiomatic: The empire is exhausted and the people are in distress; priority should go to securing the frontiers, replenishing the treasury, and preserving human resources."

sentences.zh: 后善之，召見長生殿，賞慰良厚，因是罷役。

translations.literal: The Empress approved, summoned him to the Hall of Long Life, rewarded and comforted him generously, and on this account halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was pleased, received him in the Hall of Long Life, lavished praise and gifts upon him, and halted the work.

sentences.zh: 會詔市河南河北牛羊、荊益奴婢，置監登、萊，以廣軍資。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered purchase of cattle and sheep from Henan and Hebei and bondsmen and maidservants from Jing and Yi, establishing supervisory posts at Deng and Lai to expand military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then called for buying cattle and sheep from Henan and Hebei and bondsmen from Jing and Yi, with supervisory offices at Deng and Lai to swell military stores.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上書曰：「今河南牛疫，十不一在，詔雖和市，甚於抑奪。

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial saying: "Now cattle plague afflicts Henan; fewer than one in ten remain. Though the edict speaks of fair purchase, it is worse than seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui wrote: "Henan is ravaged by cattle plague—fewer than one beast in ten survives. Though the edict speaks of fair purchase, it amounts to confiscation.

sentences.zh: 並市則價難準，簡擇則吏求賄，是牛再疫，農重傷也。

translations.literal: If all are bought together prices cannot be set fairly; if selection is made officials demand bribes—thus cattle suffer plague again and farming is gravely harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Bulk purchases make fair pricing impossible; selective buying invites official extortion—cattle die twice over and farmers are ruined.

sentences.zh: 高原耕地奪爲牧所，兩州無復丁田，牛羊踐暴，舉境何賴？

translations.literal: Highland fields are seized for pastures; the two circuits have no household fields left; cattle and sheep trample and ravage—on what can the whole region rely?
translations.idiomatic: Highland cropland is seized for pasture; the two provinces lose their household fields; cattle trample everything—what will the region live on?

sentences.zh: 荊、益奴婢多國家戸口，奸豪掠買，一入於官，永無免期。

translations.literal: Bondsmen and maidservants of Jing and Yi are mostly registered households of the state; powerful scoundrels seize and buy them; once they enter official hands there is never release.
translations.idiomatic: Most bondsmen in Jing and Yi are registered subjects; local bullies snatch them up, and once they enter government hands they are never freed.

sentences.zh: 南北異宜，至必生疾，此有損無益也。

translations.literal: North and south differ in what suits them; when they arrive illness surely arises—this harms without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: North and south have different climates; transported south or north they fall ill—pure loss, no gain.

sentences.zh: 抑聞之，君所恃在民，民所恃在食，食所資在耕，耕所資在牛；

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: what the ruler relies on is the people; what the people rely on is food; what food depends on is plowing; what plowing depends on is oxen;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard it said: a ruler depends on his people, the people on food, food on farming, and farming on oxen;

sentences.zh: 牛廢則耕廢，耕廢則食去，食去則民亡，民亡則何恃爲君？

translations.literal: if oxen are ruined then plowing is ruined, if plowing is ruined then food departs, if food departs then the people perish, if the people perish then on what can one rely as ruler?
translations.idiomatic: ruin the oxen and you ruin the plow, ruin the plow and food fails, food fails and the people die—what then is left for a ruler to stand on?

sentences.zh: 羊非軍國切要，假令蕃滋，不可射利。」

translations.literal: Sheep are not urgently needed for army and state; even if they multiply abundantly, one must not seek profit from them."
translations.idiomatic: Sheep are not vital to army or state; even if herds multiply, they should not be treated as a source of profit."

sentences.zh: 后乃止。

translations.literal: The Empress then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress relented.

sentences.zh: 張易之誅，議窮治黨與。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, discussion turned to thoroughly punishing his faction.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yizhi was put to death, the court debated rooting out his entire faction.

sentences.zh: 廷珪建言：「自古革命，務歸人心，則以刑勝治。

translations.literal: Tinggui proposed: "Since antiquity dynastic change has sought to win hearts; governing through excessive punishment prevails over true order.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui urged: "Throughout history, founding a new dynasty has meant winning hearts; rule by harsh punishment defeats true governance.

sentences.zh: 今唐歷不移，天地復主，宜以仁化蕩宥。

translations.literal: Now the Tang calendar is unbroken and Heaven and Earth have their lord again; we should use humane transformation and broad pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang line continues unbroken and the throne is restored; mercy and a broad amnesty are what is called for.

sentences.zh: 且易之盛時，趨附奔走半天下，盡誅則已暴，罰一二則法不平，宜一切洗貸。」

translations.literal: Moreover in Yizhi's heyday half the realm rushed to attach and serve; to execute all would already be excessive, to punish only one or two would make the law uneven—everything should be washed clean and forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: At the height of Yizhi's power half the empire fawned on him; mass execution would be tyranny, punishing only a few would be unfair—the whole affair should be wiped clean."

sentences.zh: 中宗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，詔白司馬阪復營佛祠，廷珪方奉詔抵河北，道出其所，見營築勞亟，懷不能已，上書切爭，且言：「自中興之初，下詔書，弛不急，斥少監楊務廉，以示中外。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong an edict ordered rebuilding the Buddhist shrine at White Sima Slope; Tinggui was on mission to Hebei, passed the site on the road, saw construction labor intense, could not restrain himself, and submitted a sharp memorial, saying: "Since the start of restoration edicts have relaxed what is not urgent and dismissed Vice Director Yang Wulian to show court and country.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era an edict revived the temple at White Sima Slope. Tinggui was traveling to Hebei on imperial business, passed the site, saw the crushing labor, and could not stay silent. He wrote urgently: "Since the restoration began, edicts have cut nonessential spending and dismissed Vice Director Yang Wulian as a signal to all.

sentences.zh: 今土木復興，不稱前詔；

translations.literal: Now earth and timber work revives—this does not match the earlier edict;
translations.idiomatic: Now construction resumes—this contradicts those edicts;

sentences.zh: 掘壤伐木，浸害生氣。

translations.literal: digging earth and felling trees gradually harms the vital breath of life.
translations.idiomatic: digging and logging steadily damage the living world.

sentences.zh: 願罷之，以紓窮乏。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be stopped to relieve destitution."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the work be halted to ease the people's want."

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 尋爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he became drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元初，大旱，關中饑，詔求直言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan under Emperor Xuanzong, great drought struck; Guanzhong suffered famine; an edict sought blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Xuanzong faced severe drought and famine in Guanzhong and called for frank advice.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏曰：「古有多難興國，殷憂啟聖，蓋事危則志銳，情苦則慮深，故能轉禍爲福也。

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial saying: "In antiquity many states rose amid hardship and deep sorrow awakened the sage—because when affairs are perilous the will is sharp and when suffering is bitter reflection is deep, thus misfortune can be turned to blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui wrote: "History shows that nations often rise from adversity and sage rulers are forged in crisis—danger sharpens resolve, suffering deepens thought, and calamity can become blessing.

sentences.zh: 景龍、先天間，兇黨構亂，陛下神武，汛掃氛垢，日月所燭，無不濡澤，明明上帝，宜錫介福。

translations.literal: Between Jinglong and Xiantian vicious factions stirred rebellion; Your Majesty's divine martial prowess swept away foul vapors; wherever sun and moon shine all are moistened with grace—clearly High Heaven should bestow great blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Through the troubles of Jinglong and Xiantian Your Majesty's valor swept away rebellion; under your radiance all are nourished—surely Heaven should grant abundant blessing.

sentences.zh: 而頃陰陽愆候，九穀失稔，關輔尤劇。

translations.literal: Yet recently yin and yang are out of season, the nine grains fail in ripening, and Guanfu suffers especially.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately the seasons have gone awry, crops have failed everywhere, and Guanzhong has suffered worst of all.

sentences.zh: 臣思天意，殆以陛下春秋鼎盛，不崇朝有大功，輕堯、舜而不法，思秦、漢以自高，故昭見咎異，欲日慎一日，永保大和，是皇天於陛下眷顧深矣，陛下得不奉若休旨而寅畏哉！

translations.literal: I reflect on Heaven's intent: perhaps because Your Majesty is in the prime of life, achieved great merit not in a single morning, lightly esteems Yao and Shun without taking them as models, and thinks of Qin and Han to exalt yourself—therefore warnings and anomalies are displayed, wishing that you grow more careful day by day and forever preserve great harmony. This is how High Heaven deeply cares for Your Majesty—should you not follow its gracious intent with reverent awe!
translations.idiomatic: I suspect Heaven means this: in your vigorous prime you achieved greatness quickly, yet you slight Yao and Shun as models while emulating the pride of Qin and Han—so Heaven shows signs of warning, urging daily caution to preserve peace. Heaven cares for you deeply; will you not heed its gracious warning with reverence?

sentences.zh: 誠願約心削志，考前王之書，敦素樸之道，登端士，放佞人，屏後宮，減外廄，場無蹴鞠之玩，野絶從禽之樂，促遠境，罷縣戍，矜惠惸獨，蠲薄徭賦，去淫巧，捐珠璧，不見可欲，使心不亂。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish that you restrain the heart and pare ambitions, examine the books of former kings, honor the way of plain simplicity, elevate upright scholars, dismiss flatterers, keep the inner palace at distance, reduce outer stables, let the grounds have no cuju games, let the wilds be rid of hunting pleasures, hasten distant borders, abolish county garrisons, show compassion to the orphaned and alone, remit light taxes and corvée, cast off extravagant craft, give up pearls and jade, let no desirable things be seen so the mind is not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to simplify your desires, study the classics of former kings, embrace plain living, promote upright men and dismiss sycophants, reduce the inner palace and imperial stables, ban ball games and hunting, shorten the frontier and end petty garrisons, aid the orphaned, lighten taxes, reject luxury and jewels, and keep temptation from your sight so your mind stays clear.

sentences.zh: 或謂天戒不足畏，而上帝馮怒，風雨迷錯，荒饉日甚，則無以濟下矣；

translations.literal: Some say heavenly warnings need not be feared—yet if High God in anger sends confused wind and rain and famine grows daily, then there is no way to aid those below;
translations.idiomatic: Some say heavenly warnings need not be feared—but if Heaven's wrath brings chaotic storms and deepening famine, how will you save your people?

sentences.zh: 或謂人窮不足恤，而億兆攜離，愁苦昏墊，則無以奉上矣。

translations.literal: some say the people's destitution need not be pitied—yet if the millions are scattered in separation, sorrow and suffering sink in darkness, then there is no way to serve what is above.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the people's misery need not concern you—but if the masses are scattered in despair, how will they support their ruler?

sentences.zh: 斯安危所系，禍福之原，奈何不察？

translations.literal: These are what security and danger depend on, the source of blessing and calamity—how can they go unexamined?
translations.idiomatic: These are the roots of safety and ruin, blessing and disaster—how can you ignore them?

sentences.zh: 今受命伊始，華夷百姓清耳以聽，刮目以視，冀有聞見，何遽孤其望哉？」

translations.literal: Now at the very start of receiving the mandate, Chinese and barbarian common people listen with cleared ears and look with widened eyes, hoping for something to hear and see—why so quickly betray their hopes?"
translations.idiomatic: You have just taken the throne; all the world listens and watches, hoping for a new beginning—why disappoint them so soon?"

sentences.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎，監察御史蔣挺坐法，詔決杖朝堂，廷珪執奏：「御史有譴，當殺殺之，不可辱也。」

translations.literal: Promoted again to vice minister of the Palace Gate, investigating censor Jiang Ting was guilty under law; an edict ordered beating with the staff in the court hall; Tinggui submitted firmly: "When a censor is at fault, if he should die then kill him—he must not be shamed."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to vice minister of the Palace Gate. When censor Jiang Ting broke the law and was ordered beaten in court, Tinggui protested: "If a censor deserves death, execute him—but do not humiliate him."

sentences.zh: 士大夫服其知體。

translations.literal: The scholar-officials admired his understanding of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired his sense of dignity.

sentences.zh: 王琚持節巡天兵諸軍，方還，復詔行塞下，議者皆謂將襲回紇，廷珪陳五不可，且言：「中國步多騎少，人齎一石糧，負甲百斤，盛夏長驅，晝夜不休，勞逸相絶，其勢不敵，一也。

translations.literal: Wang Ju held credentials to inspect the armies of Tianbing; just returned, he was again ordered to travel below the passes; discussants all said he would strike the Uyghurs; Tinggui set forth five reasons why not, saying: "Within China infantry are many and cavalry few; a man carries one stone of grain and bears armor of a hundred jin; in midsummer long drives day and night without rest—the weary and the rested are utterly apart; the situation cannot match them—first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju had inspected the Tianbing armies and barely returned when he was sent to the frontier again; many believed he would attack the Uyghurs. Tinggui listed five objections: "China has more foot soldiers than horsemen; each man carries a stone of grain and a hundred jin of armor; to drive through midsummer day and night without rest pits exhaustion against fresh mounts—we cannot win. First.

sentences.zh: 出軍掩敵，兵不數萬，不可以行，廢農廣饋，饑歳不支，二也。

translations.literal: To send troops in surprise against the enemy, if forces do not number in the tens of thousands it cannot be done; to abandon farming and broaden provisions—in famine years it cannot be sustained—second.
translations.idiomatic: A surprise campaign needs tens of thousands of men; we lack them. Abandoning farming to feed a huge army is impossible in a famine year. Second.

sentences.zh: 千里遠襲，其誰不知？

translations.literal: A strike a thousand li distant—who would not know?
translations.idiomatic: A raid a thousand li away—who will not hear of it?

sentences.zh: 賊有斥候，必能預防，三也。

translations.literal: The enemy has scouts and can surely prepare—third.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has scouts and will be ready. Third.

sentences.zh: 狄人獸居磧漠，譬之石田，克而無補，四也。

translations.literal: The barbarians dwell like beasts in desert sands—like stone fields; conquered they yield no benefit—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads live like beasts in the desert—barren ground that yields nothing even if taken. Fourth.

sentences.zh: 天下無年，當養人息兵，五也。」

translations.literal: The realm has no good harvest year; we should nurture the people and rest the armies—fifth."
translations.idiomatic: The empire has had no good harvest; we should nourish the people and keep the peace. Fifth."

sentences.zh: 又請復十道按察使，巡視州縣，帝然納之，因詔陸象先等分使十道。

translations.literal: He also asked to restore the ten-circuit inspection commissioners to tour prefectures and counties; the Emperor approved and accordingly ordered Lu Xiangxian and others to divide missions among the ten circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged restoring the ten-circuit inspection commissioners. The Emperor agreed and dispatched Lu Xiangxian and others to the ten circuits.

sentences.zh: 時遣使齎繒錦至石國市犬馬，廷珪曰：「犬馬非土性弗畜，珍禽異獸不育於國，不宜勞遠人致異物，願省無益之故，救必然之急，天下之幸。」

translations.literal: At the time envoys were sent bearing silks and brocades to the Stone Kingdom to buy dogs and horses; Tinggui said: "Dogs and horses are not of our soil and are not kept; rare birds and strange beasts are not bred in the state—it is not fitting to weary distant peoples to obtain exotic things; I wish to cut useless expenditures and rescue inevitable urgency—the fortune of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then sent with silk to buy horses in the Stone Kingdom. Tinggui said: "Dogs and horses are not native here, nor are exotic beasts bred at court. Do not trouble distant peoples for curiosities; cut useless spending and meet urgent needs—that would be the empire's blessing."

sentences.zh: 坐漏禁內語，出爲沔州刺史。

translations.literal: For leaking forbidden inner-palace speech he was demoted to prefect of Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to prefect of Mian for leaking palace secrets.

sentences.zh: 頻徙蘇、宋、魏三州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred among the three prefectures of Su, Song, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Su, Song, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，景龍中，宗楚客、紀處訥、武廷秀、韋溫等封戸多在河南、河北，諷朝廷詔兩道蠶產所宜，雖水旱得以蠶折租。

translations.literal: Earlier in Jinglong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wu Tingxiu, Wei Wen, and others had fief households mostly in Henan and Hebei; they prompted the court to decree that in the two circuits where silkworm production was suitable, even in flood or drought rent could be converted by silkworm quota.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Jinglong, Zong Chuke and others held fiefs mostly in Henan and Hebei and persuaded the court to let those circuits pay rent in silk even during drought or flood.

sentences.zh: 廷珪謂：「兩道倚大河，地雄奧，股肱走集，宜得其歡心，安可不恤其患而殫其力？

translations.literal: Tinggui said: "The two circuits lean on the great river, their land is mighty and rich, the arms and thighs of the state converge there—they should win their hearts; how can we not pity their troubles yet exhaust their strength?
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui argued: "These circuits lie along the Yellow River, the heartland where the empire's strength gathers—we should win their loyalty. How can we ignore their hardship and drain them dry?

sentences.zh: 若以桑蠶所宜而加別稅，則隴右羊馬、山南椒漆、山之銅錫鉛鍇、海之蜃蛤魚鹽，水旱皆免，寧獨河南、北外於王度哉？

translations.literal: If because mulberry and silkworm are suitable we add separate tax, then Longyou's sheep and horses, Shannan's pepper and lacquer, the mountains' copper, tin, lead, and antimony, the sea's clams, fish, and salt—all would be exempt in flood and drought; are Henan and Hebei alone outside the king's law?
translations.idiomatic: If silk regions get special treatment, why not exempt Longyou's livestock, Shannan's pepper and lacquer, mountain metals, and sea salt in every disaster? Are Henan and Hebei alone outside imperial law?

sentences.zh: 願依貞觀、永徽故事，準令折免。」

translations.literal: I wish to follow the precedents of Zhenguan and Yonghui and grant remission according to statute."
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Zhenguan and Yonghui precedents and grant statutory relief."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 在官有威化。

translations.literal: In office he had august transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: As an official he commanded respect and improved the regions he governed.

sentences.zh: 入爲少府監，封範陽縣男。

translations.literal: He entered court as director of the Palace Stores and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Palace Stores and created Baron of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as household steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as household steward of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，謚貞穆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made minister of Works; posthumous name Zhenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of Works with the posthumous name Zhenmu (Upright and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 廷珪偉姿儀，善八分書，與李邕友善，及邕躓於仕，屢表薦之，人尚其方介云。

translations.literal: Tinggui had a grand bearing, excelled at clerical script, and was friendly with Li Yong; when Yong stumbled in office he repeatedly memorialized to recommend him—people esteemed his upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui was imposing in appearance and skilled in clerical script. He was close to Li Yong and repeatedly recommended him when Yong fell from favor; people admired his principled loyalty.

sentences.zh: 韋湊，字彥宗，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Cou, style name Yanzong, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou, courtesy name Yanzong, was from Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖叔諧，貞觀中爲庫部郎中，與弟吏部郎中叔謙、兄主爵郎中季武同省，時號「三列宿」。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuxie in Zhenguan was director in the Treasury Bureau; with his younger brother Shuqian, director in the Ministry of Personnel, and elder brother Jiwu, director in the Bureau of Enfeoffment, all in one ministry, they were called "the three constellations in a row."
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuxie served as a treasury director under Zhenguan, together with his brothers in the Ministries of Personnel and Enfeoffment in the same department—they were called "the three stars in a row."

sentences.zh: 湊，永淳初，解褐婺州參軍事。

translations.literal: Cou, at the beginning of Yongchun, left the russet cloth and became military adjutant of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cou began his career in Yongchun as military adjutant of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙資州司兵，觀察使房昶才之，表於朝，遷揚州法曹。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zizhou as judicial officer for military affairs; observation commissioner Fang Chang recognized his talent, memorialized the court, and he was moved to Yangzhou as law officer.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zizhou as judicial officer, he impressed observation commissioner Fang Chang, who recommended him to court; he was promoted to law officer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州人盂神爽罷仁壽令，豪縱，數犯法，交通貴戚，吏莫敢繩，湊按治，杖殺之，遠近稱伏。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Meng Shensuang, dismissed from Renhou magistracy, was overbearing and repeatedly broke the law, associating with noble kin; officials dared not restrain him; Cou investigated, beat him to death, and near and far praised his submission.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shensuang, a dismissed magistrate and local bully who flouted the law through noble connections, was investigated by Cou, beaten to death, and the region applauded.

sentences.zh: 入爲相王府屬，時姚崇兼府長史，嘗曰：「韋子識遠文詳，吾恨晚得之。」

translations.literal: He entered as an aide of the Prince of Xiang's household; at the time Yao Chong also served as chief administrator of the princely establishment and once said: "Master Wei sees far and writes in detail—I regret obtaining him so late."
translations.idiomatic: He entered service in the household of the Prince of Xiang, where Yao Chong was chief administrator and said: "Master Wei has far-reaching judgment and careful prose—I regret not finding him sooner."

sentences.zh: 六遷司農少卿。

translations.literal: After six promotions he became vice minister of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After six promotions he became vice minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 忤宗楚客，出爲貝州刺史。

translations.literal: He offended Zong Chuke and was sent out as prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Zong Chuke and was exiled to prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，授鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne he was appointed vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Cou was made vice minister of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 徙太府，兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was moved to the Grand Treasury and concurrently served as memorial receptionist.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Grand Treasury and also served as memorial receptionist.

sentences.zh: 時改葬故太子重俊，有詔加謚，又詔雪李多祚等罪，議贈官。

translations.literal: At the time the former crown prince Chongjun was reburied; an edict added a posthumous name, and another edict cleared the crimes of Li Duozuo and others and discussed posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the late crown prince Chongjun was reburied, edicts added a posthumous title, cleared Li Duozuo and others, and debated posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 湊上言：

translations.literal: Cou submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 王者發號出令，必法大道，善善著，惡惡明也。

translations.literal: When a king issues commands he must follow the great Way—goodness made manifest, evil made clear.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's commands must follow the great Way—praising the good and exposing the wicked.

sentences.zh: 賞罰所不加，則考行立謚以褒貶之。

translations.literal: Where reward and punishment do not reach, then conduct is examined and a posthumous name is set to praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment no longer apply, conduct is judged and a posthumous name records praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 臣議其君，子議其父，曰「靈」曰「厲」者，不敢以私亂公也。

translations.literal: Ministers judge their lord, sons judge their father—calling one "Ling" or "Li" means they dare not let private feeling disorder public right.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers judge their rulers and sons their fathers—names like Ling or Li show that private feeling must not corrupt public judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見故太子與多祚等擁北軍，犯宸居，破扉斬關，兵指黃屋，騎騰紫微，和帝御玄武門親諭逆順，太子據鞍自若，督眾不止；

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that the former crown prince with Duozuo and others seized the Northern Army, violated the imperial residence, broke doors and cut gates, weapons aimed at the yellow canopy, horsemen surged at Ziwei; Emperor He personally went to Xuanwu Gate to explain rebel and loyal; the crown prince sat his saddle at ease and urged the host onward without cease;
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that the late crown prince and Duozuo seized the Northern Army, stormed the palace, broke the gates, and aimed weapons at the throne. Emperor He went to Xuanwu Gate to explain right and wrong, yet the crown prince sat calmly in his saddle and drove his troops on;

sentences.zh: 逆黨悔非，回兵執賊，多祚伏誅，太子乃遁去。

translations.literal: the rebel faction repented their error, turned troops to seize the traitors, Duozuo was executed, and only then did the crown prince flee.
translations.idiomatic: only when the rebels repented and turned on the traitors was Duozuo executed and the crown prince fled.

sentences.zh: 明日帝見群臣，涕數行下，曰：「幾不與公等相見」，其爲危甚矣！

translations.literal: Next day the Emperor saw the ministers, tears falling in streams, saying: "I nearly did not meet you again"—how grave the danger was!
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor told his ministers through tears, "I nearly never saw you again"—the danger was extreme.

sentences.zh: 臣子之禮，過位必趨，蹙路馬芻有誅。

translations.literal: The rites of subject and minister: passing the ruler's place one must hasten; trampling the road of the imperial horses' fodder is punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of subjecthood require hurrying past the ruler's seat; even trampling the fodder of the imperial horses is a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 昔漢成帝爲太子，行不敢絶馳道。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Cheng of Han was crown prince he did not dare walk across the imperial carriage road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng of Han was crown prince, he would not walk across the imperial carriage road.

sentences.zh: 秦師免胄過周北門，王孫滿策其必敗。

translations.literal: When Qin troops passed bareheaded through Zhou's north gate, Wangsun Man predicted they would surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin troops passed Zhou's north gate bareheaded, Wangsun Man predicted their defeat.

sentences.zh: 推此，則太子稱兵宮中，爲悖已甚。

translations.literal: Extending this, for the crown prince to brandish arms within the palace is already extreme perversity.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, for a crown prince to take up arms in the palace is utterly perverse.

sentences.zh: 以斬三思父子而嘉之乎，則弄兵討逆以安君父可也；

translations.literal: If we praise him for killing the father and son Sansi, then raising troops to suppress rebels and secure lord and father would suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If we honor him for killing the Sansi, then raising troops to protect the emperor would be enough;

sentences.zh: 因欲自立，則是爲逆，又奚可褒？

translations.literal: if because he wished to establish himself—then this is rebellion; how can it be praised?
translations.idiomatic: but if he sought the throne himself, that was rebellion—how can it be praised?

sentences.zh: 此時韋氏逆未明，義未絶，於太子母也，子無廢母之理；

translations.literal: At this time the Empress Wei's rebellion was not yet clear, righteous ties were not yet severed; as to the crown prince's mother, a son has no principle of deposing his mother;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wei's treason was not yet clear and familial duty was not yet broken; a son cannot depose his mother;

sentences.zh: 非中宗命廢之，則又劫父廢母。

translations.literal: unless Zhongzong ordered her deposed, this would again be coercing the father and deposing the mother.
translations.idiomatic: unless Zhongzong himself ordered it, the crown prince would merely be seizing his father and deposing his mother.

sentences.zh: 且君或不君，臣安可不臣？

translations.literal: Moreover if the lord is sometimes not lordlike, how can the minister fail to be ministerlike?
translations.idiomatic: Even if a ruler fails in his role, must not a subject still be a subject?

sentences.zh: 父或不父，子安可不子？

translations.literal: If the father is sometimes not fatherlike, how can the son fail to be sonlike?
translations.idiomatic: Even if a father fails in his role, must not a son still be a son?

sentences.zh: 晉太子申生謚曰恭，漢太子據謚曰戾，今太子乃謚節閔，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: Jin crown prince Shensheng's posthumous name was Gong; Han crown prince Ju's was Li; now the crown prince is given Jiemin—I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shensheng of Jin was posthumously Gong; Liu Ju of Han was Li; yet this crown prince is called Jiemin—I cannot understand it.

sentences.zh: 願與議謚者質於御前，使臣言非耶，甘鼎鑊之誅，申大義示天下。

translations.literal: I wish to confront those who debated the posthumous name before the throne; if my words are wrong, I gladly accept cauldron and boiling punishment; if the great principle is upheld, let it be shown to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Let me debate the namers before the throne; if I am wrong, I accept death in the cauldron; if I am right, let the great principle be shown to all.

sentences.zh: 臣言是耶，咸蒙冰釋，不復異議。

translations.literal: If my words are right, may all receive melting clarity and raise no further dispute.
translations.idiomatic: If I am right, let all doubts melt away and no one dispute further.

sentences.zh: 如曰未然，奈何使後世亂臣賊子資以爲辭？

translations.literal: If it is said this is not so, how can we let later rebellious ministers and wicked sons use it as their plea?
translations.idiomatic: If we deny this, how will we stop future traitors from using it as precedent?

sentences.zh: 宜易謚以合經禮，多祚等罪云「免」而不云「雪」。

translations.literal: The posthumous name should be changed to accord with canonical rites; Duozuo and others' crimes should say "remitted" and not "cleared."
translations.idiomatic: Change the posthumous name to fit the classics, and say Duozuo's crimes were "remitted," not "cleared."

sentences.zh: 帝瞿然，引內閣中，勞曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: The Emperor started, drew him into the inner pavilion, and said with praise: "It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor started, drew him into the inner pavilion, and said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 業已爾，奈何？」

translations.literal: The deed is already done—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The deed is done—what now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太子實逆，不可以褒，請質行以示。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The crown prince was truly rebellious and must not be praised; I beg to verify the facts and show them."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The crown prince was truly a rebel and must not be honored; let the facts be examined."

sentences.zh: 時大臣亦重改，唯罷多祚等贈官。

translations.literal: At the time the great ministers also favored revision; only Duozuo and others' posthumous offices were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers agreed to revise the decision; only Duozuo's posthumous honors were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，作金仙等觀，湊諫，以爲：「方農月興功，雖貲出公主，然高直售庸，則農人舍耕取雇，趨末棄本，恐天下有受其饑者。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun they built the Golden Immortal and other monasteries; Cou remonstrated, saying: "To raise works in the farming month—even if funds come from the princesses—high wages for hire will make farmers abandon plowing for wages, rush to the secondary and abandon the root; I fear the realm will have those who suffer hunger."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyun the court built the Golden Immortal monastery and others. Cou protested: "Construction in the planting season—even if the princesses pay—high wages will lure farmers from the fields; the realm may face famine."

sentences.zh: 不聽，湊執爭，以「萬物生育，草木昆蚑傷伐甚多，非仁聖本意」。

translations.literal: He was not heeded; Cou argued firmly that "the myriad things give birth, and grass, trees, and insects suffer great harm in felling—this is not the intent of the benevolent sage."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ignored him. Cou insisted that "countless living things are destroyed—this is not what a sage ruler intends."

sentences.zh: 帝詔外詳議。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered detailed discussion outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the matter debated openly.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔湜、侍中岑羲曰：「公敢是耶？」

translations.literal: Chief minister Cui Shi and palace attendant Cen Xi said: "Sir, do you dare to be right?
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Cui Shi and attendant Cen Xi said, "Do you really mean this?

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「食厚祿，死不敢顧，況聖世必無死乎？」

translations.literal: Cou said: "Eating thick salary, facing death I dare not look back—how much less in a sage age where death is surely not required?"
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied: "On a generous salary I cannot flinch from death—and in a sage reign I trust I will not die for speaking truth."

sentences.zh: 朝廷爲減費萬計。

translations.literal: The court reduced costs by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The court cut the budget by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 出爲陜、汝、岐三州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Shan, Ru, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Shan, Ru, and Qi in succession.

sentences.zh: 開元初，欲建碑靖陵，湊以古園陵不立碑，又云旱不可興工，諫而止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan they wished to erect a stele at Jing Mausoleum; Cou held that ancient garden tombs did not set up steles, and also said drought forbade construction; he remonstrated and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan the court planned a stele at Jing Mausoleum. Cou argued that ancient imperial tombs had no steles and that drought forbade work; the plan was halted.

sentences.zh: 遷將作大匠。

translations.literal: He was moved to grand director of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 詔復孝敬皇帝廟號義宗，湊諫曰：「傳云：『必也正名。』

translations.literal: An edict restored the temple name Yizong for the Filial and Respectful Emperor; Cou remonstrated: "The tradition says: 'One must rectify names.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the temple name Yizong for the Filial and Respectful Emperor. Cou objected: "The Analects say, 'Rectify the names.

sentences.zh: 禮：祖有功，宗有德，其廟百世不毀。

translations.literal: Rites say: ancestors with merit are zu, with virtue zong—their temples are not destroyed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The rites teach that zu honor merit and zong honor virtue—such temples endure for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 商有三宗，周宗武王，漢文帝爲太宗，武帝爲世宗。

translations.literal: Shang had three zong; Zhou made King Wu zong; Emperor Wen of Han was taizong, Emperor Wu shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang had three zong; Zhou made King Wu a zong; Han Wendi was taizong and Wudi shizong.

sentences.zh: 歷代稱宗者，皆方制海內，德澤可尊，列於昭穆，是謂不毀。

translations.literal: Dynasties that called someone zong all ruled the realm within the four seas, their virtue worthy of honor, ranked in the ancestral line—this is what "not destroyed" means.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history only rulers who pacified the realm and whose virtue merited honor were called zong and entered the ancestral temple forever.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝未嘗南面，且別立寢廟，無稱宗之義。」

translations.literal: The Filial and Respectful Emperor never faced south as ruler, and a separate sleeping temple was established—there is no meaning of calling him zong."
translations.idiomatic: The Filial and Respectful Emperor never reigned, and he already had a separate temple—he does not qualify as zong."

sentences.zh: 遂罷。

translations.literal: It was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛大將軍，玄宗謂曰：「故事，諸衛大將軍與尚書更爲之，近時職輕，故用卿以重此官，其毋辭！」

translations.literal: Promoted to general of the Right Guards, Emperor Xuanzong told him: "By precedent, generals of the guards and ministers of the Ministries alternated in the post; recently the office has been light, so I use you to weight this position—do not decline!
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to general of the Right Guards, Xuanzong said: "By custom this post alternated with ministerial rank; lately it has been slighted, so I appoint you to restore its weight—do not refuse!

sentences.zh: 尋徙河南尹，封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to mayor of Henan and enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became mayor of Henan and was created Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 會洛陽主薄王鈞以賕抵死，詔曰：「兩臺御史、河南尹縱吏侵漁，《春秋》重責帥，其出湊曹州刺史，侍御史張洽通州司馬。」

translations.literal: When Luoyang registrar Wang Jun was executed for bribery, an edict said: "Censors of both bureaus and the mayor of Henan indulged officials' oppression; the Spring and Autumn Annals hold the commander responsible—Cou is demoted to prefect of Caozhou, investigating censor Zhang Qia to army adjutant of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When registrar Wang Jun was executed for bribery, an edict blamed the censors and mayor for lax oversight: Cou was demoted to prefect of Caozhou and Zhang Qia to adjutant of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷太原尹，兼北都軍器監，邊備修舉，詔賜時服勞勉之。

translations.literal: After long service he was moved to mayor of Taiyuan and concurrently director of northern capital armories; frontier defenses were well ordered and he was granted seasonal robes in reward.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became mayor of Taiyuan and director of northern armories; the frontier was well ordered and the court rewarded him with robes of honor.

sentences.zh: 及病，遣上醫臨治。

translations.literal: When ill, the court sent the chief physician to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the chief physician was sent to attend him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈幽州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five; posthumously made military commissioner of Youzhou; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five, was posthumously made military commissioner of Youzhou, and given the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子見素。

translations.literal: His son was Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 湊子見素，字會微，質性仁厚。

translations.literal: Cou's son Jiansu, style name Huiwei, was by nature kind and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Cou's son Jiansu, courtesy name Huiwei, was gentle by nature.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，授相王府參軍，襲父爵，擢累諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi he was appointed adjutant in the Prince of Xiang's household, inherited his father's enfeoffment, and rose to remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After his jinshi degree he served in the Prince of Xiang's household, inherited his father's title, and rose to remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，爲江西、山南、黔中、嶺南道黜陟使，繩糾吏治，所至震畏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he was promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Jiangxi, Shannan, Qianzhong, and Lingnan circuits, tightening official discipline; wherever he went officials trembled.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5 he inspected Jiangxi, Shannan, Qianzhong, and Lingnan, disciplining officials so severely that all feared him.

sentences.zh: 遷文部侍郎，平判皆誦於口，銓敘平允，官有頠求，輒下意聽納，人多德之。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites, he recited all judgments from memory, conducted selection fairly, and when officials made requests he humbly listened—many thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of Rites he memorized every personnel judgment, conducted fair appointments, and graciously heard officials' requests—winning wide gratitude.

sentences.zh: 十三載，玄宗苦雨潦，閱六旬，謂宰相非其人，罷左相陳希烈，詔楊國忠審擇大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Emperor Xuanzong, vexed by sixty days of rain and floods, said the chancellor was unfit, dismissed left minister Chen Xilie, and ordered Yang Guozhong to choose a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Xuanzong, troubled by sixty days of rain, blamed the chancellor, dismissed Chen Xilie, and told Yang Guozhong to find a replacement.

sentences.zh: 時吉溫得幸，帝欲用之。

translations.literal: At the time Ji Wen had favor; the Emperor wished to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen then held imperial favor and the Emperor wished to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 溫爲安祿山所厚，國忠懼其進，沮止之。

translations.literal: Wen was close to An Lushan; Guozhong feared his rise and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen was close to An Lushan, and Guozhong blocked his appointment for fear of his influence.

sentences.zh: 謀於中書舍人竇華、宋昱，皆以見素安雅易制，國忠入白帝，帝亦以相王府屬，有舊恩，遂拜武部尚書、同中書門下平章事、集賢院學士，知門下省事。

translations.literal: He plotted with drafting secretaries Dou Hua and Song Yu; all said Jiansu was calm, elegant, and easy to control; Guozhong reported to the Emperor, who also recalled him as a former aide in the princely household with old grace—thus he was made minister of War, co-equal with the Secretariat, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and in charge of palace gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong consulted Dou Hua and Song Yu, who recommended the tractable Jiansu; citing old ties from the princely household, the Emperor made him minister of War and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 明年，祿山表請蕃將三十二人代漢將，帝許之，見素不悅，謂國忠曰：「祿山反狀暴天下，今又以蕃代漢，難將作矣。」

translations.literal: The next year Lushan memorialized asking that thirty-two barbarian generals replace Han generals; the Emperor approved; Jiansu was displeased and told Guozhong: "Lushan's rebellious intent is known to all; now replacing Han with barbarians—trouble will soon arise.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Lushan asked to replace Han generals with thirty-two non-Han commanders. The Emperor agreed. Jiansu told Guozhong, "Lushan's rebellion is obvious; this swap will bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 國忠不應，見素曰：「知禍之牙不能防，見禍之形不能制，焉用彼相？

translations.literal: Guozhong did not answer; Jiansu said: "Knowing the fang of calamity yet unable to prevent it, seeing the form of calamity yet unable to control it—of what use is such a chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was silent. Jiansu said, "You see the danger but cannot prevent it—what use is a chancellor like you?

sentences.zh: 明日當懇論之。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow I shall plead earnestly in court."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I will argue this before the throne."

sentences.zh: 既入，帝迎諭曰：「卿等有疑祿山意耶？」

translations.literal: Once inside, the Emperor greeted them saying: "Do you doubt Lushan?"
translations.idiomatic: In audience the Emperor asked, "Do you suspect Lushan?"

sentences.zh: 國忠、見素趨下，流涕具陳祿山反明甚，詔復位，因以祿山表置帝前乃出。

translations.literal: Guozhong and Jiansu hurried down, weeping and fully stating how clear Lushan's rebellion was; the edict restored their posts; they placed Lushan's memorial before the Emperor and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong and Jiansu wept and laid out Lushan's treason, had their posts restored, left his memorial before the Emperor, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝令中官袁思藝傳詔曰：「此姑忍，朕徐圖之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered eunuch Yuan Siyi to convey: "For now bear with it; I will deal with it in time."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent eunuch Yuan Siyi to say, "Bear with this for now; I will act in due course."

sentences.zh: 由是奉詔。

translations.literal: Thereafter they followed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: They obeyed.

sentences.zh: 然每進見，未嘗不爲帝言之，帝不入其語。

translations.literal: Yet whenever Jiansu attended audience he never failed to speak of it to the Emperor, who did not accept his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiansu repeated the warning at every audience, and the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，祿山反，從帝入蜀。

translations.literal: Before long Lushan rebelled; Jiansu followed the Emperor into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lushan rebelled and Jiansu followed the Emperor into Shu.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮之殺國忠也，兵傷其首，眾傳聲曰：「毋害韋公父子！」

translations.literal: When Chen Xuanli killed Guozhong, soldiers wounded Jiansu's head; the crowd shouted: "Do not harm Master Wei and his son!
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xuanli killed Guozhong, troops wounded Jiansu; the crowd cried, "Spare Master Wei and his son!

sentences.zh: 獲免。

translations.literal: He was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 帝令壽王賜藥傅創。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Prince Shou to give medicine and dress the wound.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Prince Shou send medicine and dress his wound.

sentences.zh: 次巴西，詔兼左相，封豳國公。

translations.literal: At Brazil he was ordered concurrently left minister and created Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: At Brazil he was made left minister and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，與房琯、崔渙持節奉傳國璽及冊，宣揚制命，帝曰：「太子仁孝，去十三載已有傳位意，屬方水旱，左右勸我且須豐年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, together with Fang Guan and Cui Huan he held credentials bearing the imperial seal and investiture documents to proclaim the decree; the Emperor said: "The crown prince is filial and kind; as early as the thirteenth year I already intended to pass the throne, but flood and drought came and those around me urged waiting for a good harvest year.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended, Jiansu with Fang Guan and Cui Huan bore the seal and edicts of investiture. Xuanzong said, "The crown prince is filial; I meant to abdicate as early as year 13, but floods and courtiers urged me to wait for better times.

sentences.zh: 今帝受命，朕如釋負矣。

translations.literal: Now the Emperor has received the mandate—I am as one who has laid down a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Son of Heaven has the mandate, I am relieved of my burden.

sentences.zh: 煩卿等遠去，善輔導之。」

translations.literal: I trouble you to go far—guide him well.
translations.idiomatic: Go far and guide him well.

sentences.zh: 見素涕泣拜辭，又命見素子諤及中書舍人賈至爲冊使判官，謁見肅宗於順化郡。

translations.literal: Jiansu wept and bowed in farewell; the Emperor also ordered Jiansu's son E and drafting secretary Jia Zhi as investiture commissioners' judges; they met Suzong at Shunhua commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu wept and took leave; his son E and Jia Zhi went as aides and met Suzong at Shunhua.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞琯名且舊，虛懷待之；

translations.literal: Suzong had heard Guan's name and old standing and received him with open courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, knowing Fang Guan's reputation, welcomed him warmly;

sentences.zh: 以見素嘗附國忠，禮遇獨減。

translations.literal: because Jiansu had once attached to Guozhong, his treatment alone was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: but because Jiansu had sided with Guozhong, he was treated with less honor.

sentences.zh: 是歳十月丙申，有星犯昴，見素言於帝曰：「昴者，胡也。

translations.literal: That year on the bingshen day of the tenth month a star violated the Pleiades; Jiansu said to the Emperor: "The Pleiades signify the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month on bingshen a star struck the Pleiades. Jiansu told the Emperor, "The Pleiades represent the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 天道謫見，所應在人，祿山將死矣。」

translations.literal: Heaven's way shows reproof; the response lies in men—Lushan will die."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warns; the omen falls on men—Lushan will die."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「日月可知乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Can the day and month be known?"
translations.idiomatic: Can the day be known?"

sentences.zh: 見素曰：「福應在德，禍應在刑。

translations.literal: Jiansu said: "Blessing responds to virtue, calamity to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu said, "Blessing follows virtue, calamity follows harsh rule.

sentences.zh: 昴金忌火，行當火位，昴之昏中，乃其時也。

translations.literal: The Pleiades are metal and fear fire; the cycle is entering fire; when the Pleiades are in mid-dusk—that is the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Pleiades are metal and fear fire; fire is rising; his death will come when the Pleiades are in mid-dusk.

sentences.zh: 既死其月，亦死其日。

translations.literal: He dies in that month, and dies on that day.
translations.idiomatic: He will die in that month and on that day.

sentences.zh: 明年正月申寅，祿山其殪乎！」

translations.literal: Next year on the jiayin day of the first month—will Lushan perish then?"
translations.idiomatic: Next year on jiayin of the first month—will that be Lushan's end?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「賊何等死？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How will the rebel die?"
translations.idiomatic: How will the rebel die?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「五行之説，子者視妻所生。

translations.literal: He answered: "In the theory of the five phases, the son looks to what the wife bears.
translations.idiomatic: By the five phases, the son is what the wife bears.

sentences.zh: 昴犯以丙申。

translations.literal: The violation occurred on bingshen.
translations.idiomatic: The omen came on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 金，木之妃也；

translations.literal: Metal is the consort of wood;
translations.idiomatic: Metal is wood's consort;

sentences.zh: 木，火之母也。

translations.literal: wood is the mother of fire.
translations.idiomatic: wood is fire's mother.

sentences.zh: 丙火爲金，子申亦金也。

translations.literal: Bing fire is metal; zi and shen are also metal.
translations.idiomatic: Bing fire is metal; zi and shen are metal too.

sentences.zh: 二金本同末異，還以相克，賊殆爲子與首亂者更相屠戮乎！」

translations.literal: The two metals share root but differ in branch, returning to mutual conquest—the rebel will likely be destroyed by his son and the first rebel slaughtering each other!"
translations.idiomatic: Two metals share an origin yet clash—the rebel may die by his son and fellow rebels turning on one another!"

sentences.zh: 及祿山死，日月皆驗。

translations.literal: When Lushan died, month and day both matched.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan died, month and day matched the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 明年三月至鳳翔，拜尚書右僕射，罷知政事。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month he reached Fengxiang, was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and ceased managing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he reached Fengxiang, became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and left active government.

sentences.zh: 初，行在所承喪亂後，兵吏三銓簿領煬散，選部文符僞濫，帝欲廣懷士心，至者一切補官，不加檢復。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the flight from chaos the military and civil three-selection registers were scattered and Selection Bureau documents were forged; the Emperor wished to broaden men's hearts and all who came were given office without inspection.
translations.idiomatic: After the flight, personnel records were chaotic and appointments forged; the Emperor gave office to all comers without review.

sentences.zh: 見素奏宜明條綱以爲持久，帝未及從。

translations.literal: Jiansu memorialized that clear regulations should be set for endurance; the Emperor had not yet followed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu urged clear rules for lasting order; the Emperor had not yet agreed.

sentences.zh: 既還都，選者猥集，補署無所，日訴於朝，乃追行其言。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital candidates crowded in with nowhere to appoint; daily they petitioned at court—only then was his proposal pursued.
translations.idiomatic: After the return, petitioners overwhelmed the court until his rules were enforced.

sentences.zh: 會郭子儀亦爲僕射，徙見素太子太師，詔至蜀郡奉迎太上皇。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi also became vice director, Jiansu was moved to grand preceptor of the crown prince with orders to go to Shu commandery to welcome the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi became vice director too, Jiansu was made grand preceptor and sent to Shu to welcome the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 以功食實封三百戸。

translations.literal: For merit he received three hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: He received a fief of three hundred households for his service.

sentences.zh: 上元初，以疾求致仕，許之，詔朝朔望。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan, ill, he sought retirement; it was granted; he was ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shangyuan he retired for illness but was ordered to attend on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年卒，年七十六，贈司徒，謚忠貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he died at seventy-six; posthumously made director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous name Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoying 1 at seventy-six, was posthumously director of State Affairs, and named Zhongzhen (Loyal and Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 子諤。

translations.literal: His son was E.
translations.idiomatic: His son was E.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：楊國忠本與安祿山爭寵，故捕吉溫以激其亂，陰儲蜀貲，待天子之出，則己與韋見素流涕爭祿山反狀，將信所言，以久其權。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Yang Guozhong originally vied with An Lushan for favor, so he seized Ji Wen to provoke chaos, secretly stored Shu wealth, and waited for the Son of Heaven to flee—then he and Wei Jiansu would weep and dispute Lushan's rebellion before the throne, intending that the Emperor believe them and prolong his power.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say Guozhong rivaled Lushan for favor, seized Ji Wen to stir rebellion, hoarded wealth in Shu, and waited for the emperor's flight—then he and Jiansu would weep and argue Lushan's treason so the throne would trust them and prolong Guozhong's power.

sentences.zh: 見素能言祿山反，不能言所以反，是佐國忠敗王室也，玄宗不悟，仍相之。

translations.literal: Jiansu could speak of Lushan's rebellion but not why he rebelled—this was aiding Guozhong in ruining the royal house; Emperor Xuanzong did not perceive it and still made him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu could name Lushan's rebellion but not its cause—thus he aided Guozhong in ruining the dynasty; Xuanzong never saw it and kept him as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 卒爲後帝所薄，然猶完其要領，幸矣。

translations.literal: In the end he was slighted by the later emperor, yet still preserved his essentials—fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong later slighted him, yet he kept his life and honor—fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 謂見素爲前知，果非也。

translations.literal: To call Jiansu prescient was truly not so.
translations.idiomatic: Calling Jiansu prescient was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 見素子諤歷京兆府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: Jiansu's son E served as registrar of the capital prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu's son E served as registrar of the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 國忠之死，軍聚不解，陳玄禮請殺貴妃以安眾，帝意猶豫，諤諫曰：「臣聞以計勝色者昌，以色勝計者亡。

translations.literal: After Guozhong's death the army did not disperse; Chen Xuanli asked to kill the noble consort to calm the host; the Emperor still hesitated; E remonstrated: "I have heard that he who lets strategy overcome desire prospers, he who lets desire overcome strategy perishes.
translations.idiomatic: After Guozhong's death the troops would not disband. Chen Xuanli urged killing Yang Guifei to calm them. The emperor hesitated. E said, "He who lets policy master desire survives; he who lets desire master policy perishes.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟震驚，陛下棄神器，奔草莽，惟割恩以安社稷。」

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temples are shaken, Your Majesty has abandoned the sacred vessels and fled to the wilds—only by cutting private love can the altars be secured.
translations.idiomatic: The temples are shaken, Your Majesty has fled the capital—only by sacrificing private love can the state be saved.

sentences.zh: 因叩頭流血。

translations.literal: He knocked his head until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed until it bled.

sentences.zh: 帝寤，賜妃死，軍乃大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor awoke, ordered the consort killed, and the army was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented, the consort was killed, and the army was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 擢諤御史中丞，爲置頓使。

translations.literal: E was promoted to assistant censor and made provisioning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: E was made assistant censor and provisioning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乘輿將行，或曰：「國忠死，不可往蜀，請之河、隴」，或請幸太原、朔方、涼州，或曰如京師，雜然不一。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to depart some said: "Guozhong is dead—we cannot go to Shu; let us head to He and Long," or urged Taiyuan, Shuofang, or Liangzhou, or returning to the capital—opinions were mixed.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to flee, some said Shu was unsafe and urged He-Long, Taiyuan, Shuofang, Liangzhou, or even the capital—opinions clashed.

sentences.zh: 帝心向蜀，未能言。

translations.literal: The Emperor's heart inclined to Shu but he could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Shu but could not say so.

sentences.zh: 諤曰：「今兵少，不能捍賊，還京非萬全計，不如至扶風，徐圖去就。」

translations.literal: E said: "Now troops are few and cannot resist the rebels; returning to the capital is not a plan of perfect safety—better go to Fufeng and consider the next move slowly."
translations.idiomatic: E said, "We are too few to fight; the capital is unsafe—better pause at Fufeng and decide later."

sentences.zh: 帝問於眾，眾然之，遂至扶風，乃決西幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the crowd; all agreed; they reached Fufeng and then resolved to go west.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed; they reached Fufeng, then set out for Shu.

sentences.zh: 後終給事中。

translations.literal: Later he ended as supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later became supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 諤從子顗，字周仁，諤弟益之子。

translations.literal: E's nephew Yan, style name Zhouren, was son of E's younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: E's nephew Yan, courtesy name Zhouren, was the son of E's brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，事姊恭順。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he served his elder sister with respectful obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his elder sister with filial care.

sentences.zh: 及長，身不衣帛。

translations.literal: When grown he did not wear silk himself.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he wore no silk.

sentences.zh: 通陰陽象緯，博知山川風俗，論議曲據。

translations.literal: He mastered yin-yang, omens, and geography and customs, arguing with detailed evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered astrology, geography, and customs and argued with precise evidence.

sentences.zh: 以門調補千牛備身。

translations.literal: By family standing he was made armed attendant of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: By family rank he became an armed attendant of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 自鄠尉判入等，授萬年尉。

translations.literal: From E county assistant he entered the upper grade and was appointed wannian assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: From assistant magistrate of E he entered the upper grade and became assistant magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 歷御史、補闕，與李約、李正辭更進諷諫，數移大事。

translations.literal: He served as censor and remonstrator, with Li Yue and Li Zhengzhi taking turns in admonition, repeatedly moving great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor and remonstrator with Li Yue and Li Zhengzhi, repeatedly shaping major policy.

sentences.zh: 裴垍、韋貫之、李絳、崔群、蕭俯皆布衣舊，繼爲宰相，朝廷典章多所咨逮，嘗曰：「吾儕五人，智不及一韋公。」

translations.literal: Pei Ji, Wei Guanzhi, Li Jiang, Cui Qun, and Xiao Fu were all old friends from commoner days who in succession became chancellors; the court's statutes were much consulted with him; they once said: "We five in wisdom do not equal one Master Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, Wei Guanzhi, Li Jiang, Cui Qun, and Xiao Fu—commoner friends who became chancellors—often sought his counsel and said, "Our five minds together do not equal one Master Wei."

sentences.zh: 長慶初爲大理少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing he became vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，授御史中丞，爲戸部侍郎，徙吏部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne he was made assistant censor, vice minister of Revenue, then moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingzong he became assistant censor, vice minister of Revenue, then Personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 所著《易縕解》，推演終始，有深誼。

translations.literal: His work Explication of the Changes in Silk Cord, tracing beginning and end, has profound meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His Explication of the Changes traces cosmic cycles with deep insight.

sentences.zh: 既喜接士，後出莫不造門。

translations.literal: He delighted in receiving scholars; those who later rose all visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed scholars; future luminaries all called at his door.

sentences.zh: 而李逢吉方結黨與，擅國政，頗傅會之，素議遂衰。

translations.literal: But Li Fengji was then forming factions and monopolizing government, largely courting him, and his pure reputation declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Fengji was building a faction and courting him, and his moral standing faded.

sentences.zh: 然節儉自居，天下推其尚云。

translations.literal: Yet he lived frugally by himself, and the realm praised his standards.
translations.idiomatic: He still lived frugally, and the world admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 見素從子知人，字行哲，叔謙子。

translations.literal: Jiansu's nephew Zhiren, style name Xingzhe, was son of Shuqian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu's nephew Zhiren, courtesy name Xingzhe, was Shuqian's son.

sentences.zh: 弱而好古。

translations.literal: Weak in years but fond of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Frail in youth, he loved antiquity.

sentences.zh: 以國子舉授校書郎。

translations.literal: Recommended through the Directorate of Education he was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Directorate of Education he became a collator.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，擢州參軍八人爲中臺郎，知人自荊府兵曹遷司庫員外郎，兼判司戎大夫事。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong eight prefectural adjutants were raised to central platform officers; Zhiren moved from Jing prefecture military adjutant to outer director in the Treasury Bureau and concurrently judged affairs of the Directorate of Military Horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong promoted eight prefectural adjutants to central posts; Zhiren went from Jing military adjutant to treasury outer director and judged military horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 子維、繩。

translations.literal: His sons were Wei and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wei and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 知人子維，字文紀。

translations.literal: Zhiren's son Wei, style name Wenji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren's son Wei, courtesy name Wenji.

sentences.zh: 進士對策高第，擢武功主簿。

translations.literal: In the jinshi policy examination he placed in the top grade and was made chief clerk of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the jinshi policy exam and became chief clerk of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 督役乾陵，會歳饑，均力勸功，人不知勞。

translations.literal: Supervising labor at Qian Mausoleum, famine came; he equalized strength and urged achievement so people did not feel toil.
translations.idiomatic: Overseeing work at Qian Mausoleum during famine, he balanced labor so people scarcely felt the burden.

sentences.zh: 坐徐敬業親，貶五泉主簿。

translations.literal: Because he was kin to Xu Jingye he was demoted to chief clerk of Wuquan.
translations.idiomatic: As kin to Xu Jingye he was demoted to chief clerk of Wuquan.

sentences.zh: 徙內江令，教民耕桑，縣爲刻頌。

translations.literal: Moved to magistrate of Neijiang, he taught the people farming and sericulture; the county carved a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Neijiang he taught farming and sericulture; the county erected a praise stele.

sentences.zh: 遷戸部郎中，善裁剖，時員外宋之問善詩，故時稱「戸部二妙」。

translations.literal: Promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, skilled in judgment; at the time outer director Song Zhiwen excelled in poetry, so they were called "the two wonders of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: As Revenue director he judged well; with poet Song Zhiwen as outer director they were called "Revenue's two marvels."

sentences.zh: 終太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He ended as right assistant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as right assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 知人子繩，長文辭。

translations.literal: Zhiren's son Sheng was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren's son Sheng excelled at prose.

sentences.zh: 撫養宗屬孤幼無異情。

translations.literal: He raised orphaned kin of the clan with no difference in affection.
translations.idiomatic: He raised clan orphans as tenderly as his own children.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，以母老不肯仕。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he would not serve because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he refused office while his mother lived.

sentences.zh: 逾二十年，乃歷長安尉，威行京師。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years he finally served as wannian assistant magistrate, and his authority prevailed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years he became wannian assistant magistrate and commanded respect in the capital.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，更泗、涇、鄜三州刺史。

translations.literal: Raised to investigating censor, he served in succession as prefect of Si, Jing, and Zou.
translations.idiomatic: He became investigating censor and prefect of Si, Jing, and Zou in turn.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，入爲秘書少監，玄宗尚文，視其職如尚書丞、郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he entered as vice director of the Secretariat; Emperor Xuanzong valued literature and treated the post like a director or bureau chief in the Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he became vice director of the Secretariat; Xuanzong valued letters and treated the post like a high ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 繩刊是圖簡，以善職稱。

translations.literal: Sheng collated the archive registers and was praised for competent service.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng collated the archives and won praise for competent service.

sentences.zh: 終陳王傅。

translations.literal: He ended as tutor of the Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as tutor to the Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 知人孫虛心，字無逸，維子。

translations.literal: Zhiren's grandson Xuxin, style name Wuyi, was son of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren's grandson Xuxin, courtesy name Wuyi, was Wei's son.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞、侍御史。

translations.literal: Promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant director of Judicial Review and attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，按大獄，僕射竇懷貞、侍中劉幽求有所輕重，虛心據正不橈。

translations.literal: In Shenlong he investigated a great case; Director Dou Huai Zhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu showed partiality, but Xuxin held to the right without bending.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong he investigated a major case; Dou Huai Zhen and Liu Youqiu showed bias, but Xuxin held firm.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，屬羌叛，既禽捕，有詔悉誅，虛心惟論酋長死，原活其餘。

translations.literal: In Jinglong when Qiang rebels were captured an edict ordered all executed; Xuxin argued only chieftains should die and the rest be spared.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong, when captured Qiang rebels were ordered executed, Xuxin argued only chiefs should die and the rest live.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to assistant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became assistant censor.

sentences.zh: 歷荊、潞、揚三大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He served as chief administrator of the three great military commissions of Jing, Lu, and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was chief administrator at Jing, Lu, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 荊州有鄕豪，負勢干法，虛心籍其訾入之官。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou a rural magnate relied on power to defy the law; Xuxin registered his assets for the government.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhou he seized a magnate's assets who had defied the law.

sentences.zh: 以廬江多盜，遂縣舒城，盜賊爲衰。

translations.literal: Because Lujiang had many bandits he established the county seat at Shucheng and banditry declined.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the Lujiang seat to Shucheng and banditry fell.

sentences.zh: 入爲工部尚書、東京留守。

translations.literal: He entered as minister of Works and eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of Works and eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 累封南皮郡子卒，贈揚州大都督，謚曰正。

translations.literal: Repeatedly enfeoffed Baron of Nanpi, he died; posthumously made military commissioner of Yangzhou; posthumous name Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed Baron of Nanpi, he died, was posthumously military commissioner of Yangzhou, and named Zheng (Upright).

sentences.zh: 弟虛舟，歷洪、魏二州刺史，有治名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xuzhou served as prefect of Hong and Wei and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xuzhou governed Hong and Wei with distinction.

sentences.zh: 入爲刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered as vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 初，維爲郎，蒔柳於廷，及虛心兄弟居郎省，對之輒斂容。

translations.literal: Earlier when Wei was a bureau officer he planted willows in the courtyard; when the Xuxin brothers served in the bureau they always composed themselves before them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was an officer he planted willows in the courtyard; the Xuxin brothers always composed themselves before them in office.

sentences.zh: 自叔謙後，至郎中者數人，世號「郎官家」。

translations.literal: From Shuqian onward several reached bureau chief; the age called them "the Bureau Officer family."
translations.idiomatic: From Shuqian on several became bureau chiefs—the "Bureau Officer family."

sentences.zh: 韓思復，字紹出，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Han Sifu, style name Shaochu, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sifu, courtesy name Shaochu, was from Chang'an in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖倫，貞觀中歷左衛率，封長山縣男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lun in Zhenguan served as left guard commander and was enfeoffed Baron of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lun served as left guard commander under Zhenguan and was Baron of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 思復少孤，年十歳，母爲語父亡狀，感咽幾絶，故倫特愛之，嘗曰：「此兒必大吾宗。」

translations.literal: Sifu was orphaned young; at ten his mother told how his father died; he sobbed nearly to death, so Lun especially loved him and once said: "This boy will enlarge our clan."
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, at ten he wept hearing how his father died; Lun loved him and said, "This boy will glorify our house."

sentences.zh: 然家富有，金玉、車馬、玩好未嘗省。

translations.literal: Yet the family was wealthy and he never counted gold, jade, carriages, horses, or curios.
translations.idiomatic: Though wealthy, he never counted luxuries.

sentences.zh: 篤學，舉秀才高第，襲祖封。

translations.literal: He studied deeply, passed the xiucai examination in the top grade, and inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted student, he topped the xiucai exam and inherited his grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，家益窶，歳饑，京兆杜瑾者，以百綾餉思復，思復方並日食，而綾完封不發。

translations.literal: In Yongchun the family grew poorer; famine came; Du Jin of the capital sent a hundred bolts of silk to Sifu; Sifu was eating every other day yet the silk remained sealed unopened.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun the family grew poor; Du Jin sent a hundred bolts of silk while Sifu ate every other day yet never opened the gift.

sentences.zh: 調梁府倉曹參軍，會大旱，輒開倉賑民，州劾責，對曰：「人窮則濫，不如因而活之，無趣爲盜賊。」

translations.literal: Assigned as granary adjutant of Liang prefecture, great drought came; he opened the granary to relieve the people; the prefecture impeached him; he replied: "When people are desperate they turn to excess—better revive them than drive them to become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: As Liang granary adjutant he opened stores in drought; impeached, he said, "Desperate people turn to crime—feed them rather than make bandits."

sentences.zh: 州不能詘。

translations.literal: The prefecture could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture could not answer.

sentences.zh: 轉汴州司戸，仁恕，不行鞭罰。

translations.literal: Transferred to Bianzhou revenue officer, he was humane and forbearing and did not use the whip.
translations.idiomatic: As Bianzhou revenue officer he was merciful and never used the whip.

sentences.zh: 以親喪去官，鬻薪自給。

translations.literal: He left office for parental mourning and sold firewood to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn and sold firewood to live.

sentences.zh: 姚崇爲夏官侍郎，識之，擢司禮博士。

translations.literal: Yao Chong as vice minister of Summer Offices recognized him and raised him to doctor of the Directorate of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong recognized him and made him a rites doctor.

sentences.zh: 五遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Five promotions to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose five times to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建昌王武攸寧母亡，請鼓吹，思復持不可而止。

translations.literal: When the mother of Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning died he requested imperial music; Sifu held that it could not be and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Youning's mother died he demanded imperial music; Sifu refused and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 坐爲王同皎所薦，貶始州長史。

translations.literal: Because he was recommended by Wang Tongjiao he was demoted to chief administrator of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Wang Tongjiao, he was demoted to chief administrator of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷滁州刺史，州有銅官，人鏟鑿尤苦，思復爲賈他鄙，費省獲多。

translations.literal: Moved to prefect of Chuzhou; the prefecture had copper offices and people's mining was especially bitter; Sifu had goods bought from other districts, saving expense and gaining more.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Chuzhou he eased copper mining labor by buying elsewhere, saving cost and increasing yield.

sentences.zh: 有黃芝五生州署，民爲刻頌其祥。

translations.literal: Five yellow fungi grew at the prefectural office; the people carved a eulogy to its auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Five yellow fungi grew at his yamen; the people praised the omen.

sentences.zh: 徙襄州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入拜給事中。

translations.literal: He entered court as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝作景龍觀，思復諫曰：「禍難初弭，土木遽興，非憂物恤人所急。」

translations.literal: The Emperor built Jinglong Abbey; Sifu remonstrated: "Calamity has just been quelled yet earth and timber rise in haste—this is not what cherishing things and pitying people urgently requires."
