translations.idiomatic: When the emperor built Jinglong Abbey, Sifu protested: "Disaster has barely ended—construction is not what the people need."

sentences.zh: 不見省。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was ignored.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思坐譙王重福事，捕送詔獄，有司劾善思「任汝州刺史，與王游；

translations.literal: Yan Shansi was implicated in Prince of Qiao Chongfu's affair, seized and sent to the edict prison; the officials impeached Shansi: "While prefect of Ruzhou he associated with the prince;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi was implicated with Prince Chongfu of Qiao and jailed; officials charged that as prefect of Ruzhou he associated with the prince;

sentences.zh: 至京師，不暴王謀，但奏東都有兵氣。

translations.literal: reaching the capital he did not expose the prince's plot but only memorialized that the eastern capital had a military aura.
translations.idiomatic: in the capital he hid the plot and only reported military omens in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 匿反罔上，宜伏誅」。

translations.literal: Concealing rebellion and deceiving the sovereign—he should be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Concealing rebellion—he should die."

sentences.zh: 思復曰：「往韋氏擅內，謀危社稷，善思詣相府，白陛下必即位。

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Formerly when the Wei clan dominated the inner palace and plotted against the altars, Shansi went to the chief minister's office and declared that Your Majesty would surely take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said, "When the Wei clan threatened the throne, Shansi told the chief minister you would surely reign.

sentences.zh: 今詔追善思，書發即至，使有逆節者，肯遽奔命哉？

translations.literal: Now the edict recalls Shansi and the letter sent he at once arrives—if he had rebellious intent would he rush to obey?
translations.idiomatic: Now he comes at once when summoned—would a rebel obey so quickly?

sentences.zh: 請集百官議。」

translations.literal: I beg to assemble the hundred officials to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Let the officials debate."

sentences.zh: 議多同，善思得免死，流靜州。

translations.literal: Most agreed; Shansi escaped death and was exiled to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Most agreed; Shansi was exiled to Jingzhou instead of executed.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，數指言得失，頗見納用。

translations.literal: Promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat, he repeatedly pointed out gains and losses and was largely accepted.
translations.idiomatic: As drafting secretary he often criticized policy and was largely heeded.

sentences.zh: 開元初，爲諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 山東大蝗，宰相姚崇遣使分道捕瘞。

translations.literal: Great locusts struck Shandong; Chancellor Yao Chong sent envoys on separate routes to capture and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged Shandong; Yao Chong sent envoys to capture and bury them.

sentences.zh: 思復上言：「夾河州縣，飛蝗所至，苗輒盡，今游食至洛。

translations.literal: Sifu submitted: "Prefectures and counties along the river—where flying locusts pass seedlings are instantly gone; now they roam feeding as far as Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu wrote, "Along the Yellow River crops vanish where locusts pass; they now reach Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 使者往來，不敢顯言。

translations.literal: Envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys dare not speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 且天災流行，庸可盡瘞？

translations.literal: Moreover when heavenly disaster spreads, how can all be buried?
translations.idiomatic: When disaster spreads, how can burial solve it?

sentences.zh: 望陛下悔過責躬，損不急之務，任至公之人，持此誠實以答譴咎，其驅蝗使一切宜罷。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will repent and blame yourself, cut nonurgent affairs, employ utterly fair men, hold this sincerity to answer reproof, and abolish all locust-driving commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: Repent, cut nonessential spending, appoint fair men, answer Heaven sincerely, and abolish the locust commissioners."

sentences.zh: 玄宗然之，出其疏付崇，崇建遣思復使山東按所損，還，以實言。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong approved, gave his memorial to Chong, and Chong promptly sent Sifu to Shandong to inspect damage; returning, he spoke truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong agreed, gave the memorial to Chong, who sent Sifu to inspect Shandong; he reported truthfully.

sentences.zh: 崇又遣監察御史劉沼覆視，沼希宰相意，悉易故牒以聞，故河南數州賦不得蠲。

translations.literal: Chong again sent investigating censor Liu Zhao to re-inspect; Zhao curried the chancellor's favor and changed all the old records in reporting, so several Henan prefectures' taxes could not be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent Liu Zhao to verify; Zhao flattered the chancellor and falsified records, denying tax relief to Henan.

sentences.zh: 崇惡之，出爲德州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong disliked him and sent him out as prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong disliked him and exiled him to Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝北巡，爲行在巡問賑給大使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the north he was mobile-court inquiry and relief commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern tour he directed relief for the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫，性恬淡，不喜爲繩察，徙太子賓客，進爵伯。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor-in-chief; by nature calm and indifferent, he disliked strict investigation; moved to guest of the crown prince and advanced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: Made censor-in-chief, he was calm and disliked harsh scrutiny; he became crown prince's guest and baron.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 復爲襄州刺史，治行名天下，代還，仍拜太子賓客。

translations.literal: Again prefect of Xiangzhou, his governance was famed throughout the realm; when replaced he was again made guest of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Again prefect of Xiangzhou, famed for governance, he returned as crown prince's guest.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four with posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 天子親題其碑曰「有唐忠孝韓長山之墓」。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven personally inscribed his stele: "Tomb of Han Changshan, loyal and filial of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed his stele: "Tomb of Han Changshan, loyal and filial of Tang."

sentences.zh: 故吏盧僎、邑人孟浩然立石峴山。

translations.literal: Former subordinate Lu Qian and townsman Meng Haoran set a stone on Mount Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian and Meng Haoran erected a stone on Mount Xian.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭仁傑、李無爲者，隱居太白山，思復少從二人游，嘗曰：「子識清貌古，恨仕不及宰相也。」

translations.literal: Earlier Zheng Renjie and Li Wuwei lived in seclusion on Taibai Mountain; Sifu in youth followed the two in study and once said: "Your insight is clear and your bearing ancient—I regret your office did not reach chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Youthfully he studied with hermits Zheng Renjie and Li Wuwei and said, "You are wise and grave—I regret you never reached the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 子朝宗。

translations.literal: His son was Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 思復子朝宗，初歷左拾遺。

translations.literal: Sifu's son Chaozong first served as left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu's son Chaozong first served as left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 睿宗詔作乞寒胡戲，諫曰：「昔辛有過伊川，見被發而祭，知其必戎。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong ordered the Cold Food Barbarian play; he remonstrated: "Formerly Xin You passed Yichuan, saw disheveled hair in sacrifice, and knew barbarians would surely come.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong ordered the Cold Food Barbarian play; Chaozong objected: "Xin You saw disheveled sacrifice at Yichuan and knew barbarians would come.

sentences.zh: 今乞寒胡，非古不法，無乃爲狄？

translations.literal: Now the Cold Food Barbarian is not ancient and not law—might it not be Di?
translations.idiomatic: This play is neither ancient nor lawful—will it not breed barbarian ways?

sentences.zh: 又道路藉藉，咸言皇太子微服觀之。

translations.literal: Moreover the roads are noisy with talk that the crown prince watches in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors say the crown prince watches in disguise.

sentences.zh: 且匈奴在邸，刺客卒發，大憂不測，白龍魚服，深可畏也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Xiongnu are in the lodge; assassins may strike suddenly—great worry and uncertainty; the white dragon in fish garb is deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu embassy is here—assassins may strike; a ruler in disguise is perilous.

sentences.zh: 況天象變見，疫癘相仍，厭兵助陰，是謂無益。」

translations.literal: Moreover heavenly signs change and epidemics follow in succession; war-weariness aids yin—this is called without benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Omens multiply and plague spreads; war-weariness feeds yin—this does no good."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，特賜中上考。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him and specially granted a middle-upper evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and gave a top evaluation.

sentences.zh: 帝傳位太子，朝宗與將軍龐承宗諫曰：「太子雖睿聖，宜且養成盛德。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor transmitted the throne to the crown prince, Chaozong with General Pang Chengzong remonstrated: "Though the crown prince is wise and sage, he should still be nurtured to complete virtue."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor abdicated to the crown prince, Chaozong and Pang Chengzong urged, "The crown prince is wise but still needs time to mature."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 累遷荊州長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年，初置十道採訪使，朝宗以襄州刺史兼山南東道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan the ten-circuit investigation commissioners were first established; Chaozong as prefect of Xiangzhou concurrently held Shannan East.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22 the ten-circuit commissioners were created; Chaozong held Xiangzhou and Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 襄州南楚故城有昭王井，傳言汲者死，行人雖暍困，不敢視，朝宗移書諭神，自是飲者亡恙，人更號韓公井。

translations.literal: In Xiangzhou's old city of Southern Chu there was Prince Zhao's Well; legend said those who drew water died; travelers though thirsty and weary dared not look; Chaozong sent a letter instructing the spirit, and thereafter drinkers were unharmed; people renamed it Master Han's Well.
translations.idiomatic: At Prince Zhao's Well in Xiangzhou, rumored deadly, Chaozong wrote to the spirit; drinkers were safe thereafter, and it was renamed Master Han's Well.

sentences.zh: 坐所任吏擅賦役，貶洪州刺史。

translations.literal: Because officials he appointed levied corvée on their own he was demoted to prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates levied taxes illegally; he was demoted to prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，召爲京兆尹，分渭水入金光門，匯爲潭，以通西市材木。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was summoned as mayor of the capital, divided the Wei River into Jinguang Gate, pooled it into a pond, and opened passage for timber from the western market.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he became capital mayor, diverted the Wei through Jinguang Gate into a pond to float timber for the western market.

sentences.zh: 出爲高平太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as grand administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 始，開元末，海內無事，訛言兵當興，衣冠潛爲避世計，朝宗廬終南山，爲長安尉霍仙奇所發，玄宗怒，使侍御史王訊之。

translations.literal: At first, by the end of Kaiyuan the realm was at peace; false talk said war would rise; officials secretly planned escape; Chaozong built a hut on Zhongnan Mountain and was reported by Chang'an assistant magistrate Huo Xianqi; Emperor Xuanzong was angry and sent attendant censor Wang Xun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyuan, rumors of war drove officials to hide; Chaozong retired to Zhongnan Mountain; reported by Huo Xianqi, he was investigated by Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 貶吳興別駕，卒。

translations.literal: Demoted to vice-prefect of Wuxing, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to Wuxing vice-prefect, he died.

sentences.zh: 朝宗喜識拔後進，嘗薦崔宗之、嚴武於朝，當時士咸歸重之。

translations.literal: Chaozong delighted in recognizing and promoting the young; he once recommended Cui Zongzhi and Yan Wu to court; scholars of the time all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong promoted younger talent, recommending Cui Zongzhi and Yan Wu; scholars esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 朝宗孫佽，字相之，性清簡。

translations.literal: Chaozong's grandson Ci, style name Xiangzhi, was by nature pure and simple.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's grandson Ci, courtesy name Xiangzhi, was plain and upright.

sentences.zh: 元和初第進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree early in Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 自山南東道使府入爲殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: From the Shannan East circuit envoy's staff he entered as attendant censor in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace attendant censor from Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 累遷桂管觀察使，部二十餘州，自參軍至縣令無慮三百員，吏部所補才十一，餘皆觀察使商才補職。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted observation commissioner of Guiguan, over twenty prefectures—from adjutant to magistrate nearly three hundred posts—the Ministry of Personnel supplied only eleven; the rest the observation commissioner chose by private judgment.
translations.idiomatic: As Guiguan commissioner over twenty prefectures, he found only eleven of three hundred posts filled by the Ministry; the rest were patronage appointments.

sentences.zh: 佽下車，悉來謁，一吏持籍請補缺員，佽下教曰：「居官治，吾不奪；

translations.literal: When Ci took office all came to pay respects; one clerk held the register asking to fill vacancies; Ci issued instruction: "In office govern well—I will not remove you;
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, Ci told petitioners: "Serve well and keep your post;

sentences.zh: 其不奉法，無望縱舍。

translations.literal: if you do not follow the law, do not hope for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: break the law and expect no mercy.

sentences.zh: 缺者，須按籍取可任任之。」

translations.literal: For vacancies, take the register and appoint those fit to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Fill vacancies only from qualified men on the register.

sentences.zh: 會春服使至，鄕有豪猾厚進賄使者，求爲縣令，使者請佽，佽許之。

translations.literal: When the spring-robes envoy arrived, a rural bully advanced heavy bribes to the envoy seeking a magistracy; the envoy asked Ci, and Ci consented.
translations.idiomatic: A bully bribed the spring-robes envoy for a magistracy; Ci agreed.

sentences.zh: 既去，召鄕豪責以橈法，笞其背，以令部中，自是豪右畏戢。

translations.literal: After the man left, Ci summoned the bully and charged him with bending the law, flogged his back, and made it known in the circuit—thereafter the powerful feared and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ci then summoned and flogged the bully for corruption, and the powerful feared him thereafter.

sentences.zh: 時詔置五管監兵，盡境賦不足充其費，佽處以儉約，遂爲定制，眾以爲難。

translations.literal: At the time an edict set five-circuit supervisory troops; border levies could not cover the cost; Ci managed with frugality and it became fixed practice—people thought it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When border levies could not fund five-circuit troops, Ci's frugality became standard—admired as difficult.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宋務光，字子昂，一名烈，汾州西河人。

translations.literal: Song Wuguang, style name Zi'ang, also named Lie, was a man of Xihe in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wuguang, courtesy name Zi'ang, also called Lie, was from Xihe in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士及第，調洛陽尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as Luoyang assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and became Luoyang assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛騎曹參軍。

translations.literal: Promoted to adjutant of the Right Guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Guard cavalry adjutant.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，大水，詔文武九品以上官直言極諫，務光上書曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong great flood came; an edict ordered civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above to speak bluntly to the utmost; Wuguang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1, after flood, Wuguang submitted a blunt memorial:

sentences.zh: 後王樂聞過，罔不興；

translations.literal: Later kings delight in hearing of faults—none fail to rise; reject remonstrance—none fail to fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Kings who welcome criticism prosper; those who reject it fall.

sentences.zh: 拒諫，罔不亂。

translations.literal: Reject remonstrance—none fail to fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Reject remonstrance—none fail to fall.

sentences.zh: 樂聞過則下情通，下情通則政無缺，此所以興也。

translations.literal: Delight in hearing faults and lower sentiment flows through; lower sentiment flowing, government has no gaps—this is how one rises.
translations.idiomatic: Welcome criticism and the people's voice reaches you—government has no gaps—thus comes prosperity.

sentences.zh: 拒諫則群議壅，群議壅則上孤立，此所以亂也。

translations.literal: Reject remonstrance and group opinion is blocked; group opinion blocked and the ruler stands alone—this is how disorder comes.
translations.idiomatic: Block remonstrance and the ruler stands alone—thus comes disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗觀天人相與之際，有感必應，其間甚密，是以教失於此，變生於彼。

translations.literal: I have observed the juncture of Heaven and man: where there is feeling there is response—the interval is very close; thus teaching lost here, change is born there.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and man respond to each other; moral failure here brings calamity there.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉兇，聖人象之。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven hangs images, revealing fortune and misfortune; the sage images them.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says Heaven displays omens and sages interpret them.

sentences.zh: 竊見自夏以來，水氣勃戾，天下多罹其災，洛水暴漲，漂損百姓。

translations.literal: I have seen since summer that water's qi is violent; the realm suffers much disaster; the Luo River surged and harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Since summer water has turned violent; the Luo flooded and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「簡宗廟，廢祠祀，則水不潤下。」

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Simplify ancestral temples and abolish sacrifices, then water will not moisten below.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says: neglect temples and sacrifices, and waters will not subside.

sentences.zh: 夫王者即位，必郊祀天地，嚴配祖宗。

translations.literal: When a king takes the throne he must sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and solemnly match the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: A new ruler must sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and ancestors.

sentences.zh: 自陛下御極，郊、廟、山川不時薦見。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty assumed the throne, suburban, temple, and mountain sacrifices are not offered in season.
translations.idiomatic: Since your accession, sacrifices have not been offered in season.

sentences.zh: 又水者陰類，臣妾之道，氣盛則水泉溢，頃虹蜺紛錯，暑雨滯霪，陰勝之沴也。

translations.literal: Moreover water is yin; it is the way of consorts and subjects; when qi is strong springs overflow; recently rainbows crisscross and summer rains linger—yin overcomes.
translations.idiomatic: Water is yin, the way of consorts; excessive yin brings floods and lingering rains.

sentences.zh: 後廷近習或有離中饋之職以幹外政，願深思天變，杜絶其萌。

translations.literal: Those near in the inner court may leave the inner kitchen's duty to meddle in outer government—I beg deep reflection on heaven's changes and cutting the sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Court favorites meddle in government—cut this off at the root.

sentences.zh: 又自春及夏，牛多病死，疫氣浸淫。

translations.literal: Moreover from spring to summer many cattle died and pestilence spread.
translations.idiomatic: From spring to summer cattle died and pestilence spread.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「思之不睿，時則有牛禍。」

translations.literal: The tradition says: "When reflection is not clear, then cattle calamity comes.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says unclear governance brings cattle plague.

sentences.zh: 意者萬機之事，陛下未躬親乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty not personally attend the myriad affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not personally govern?

sentences.zh: 晁錯曰：「五帝其臣不及，則自親之。」

translations.literal: Chao Cuo said: "The Five Emperors' ministers could not match them, so they personally acted.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo said even the Five Emperors ruled in person when ministers fell short.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷賢佐雖多，然莫能仰陛下清光。

translations.literal: Now the court has many worthy assistants, yet none can face Your Majesty's clear radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The court has talent, yet none can reach you.

sentences.zh: 願勤思法宮，凝就大化。

translations.literal: I beg diligent thought in the law palace and congealing great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Rule from the law palace and complete great transformation.

sentences.zh: 以萬方爲念，不以聲色爲娛；

translations.literal: Take the myriad regions as thought, not sound and color as pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: Think of the realm, not pleasure;

sentences.zh: 以百姓爲憂，不以犬馬爲樂。

translations.literal: take the hundred surnames as worry, not dogs and horses as joy.
translations.idiomatic: worry for the people, not hounds and horses.

sentences.zh: 臣聞三五之君不能免淫亢，顧備御存乎人耳。

translations.literal: I hear that even the Three Five rulers could not avoid excess and drought—only preparation in men matters.
translations.idiomatic: Even sage rulers faced disaster—preparation in men matters.

sentences.zh: 災興細微，安之不怪，及禍變已成，駭而圖之，猶水決治防、病困求藥，雖復人黽俯，尚何救哉！

translations.literal: Calamity begins subtle; if one is calm at strangeness, when catastrophe forms and one is alarmed and schemes—it is like repairing a dike after flood, seeking medicine when illness is deep; though men strive, how can it be saved!
translations.idiomatic: Ignore small signs and react too late—like mending dikes after flood.

sentences.zh: 夫塞變應天，實系人事。

translations.literal: Blocking change and answering Heaven truly lies in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Answering Heaven lies in human conduct.

sentences.zh: 今霖雨即閉坊門，豈一坊一市能感發天道哉？

translations.literal: Now in heavy rain you close ward gates—can one ward and one market move Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Closing ward gates in rain cannot move Heaven.

sentences.zh: 必不然矣。

translations.literal: Surely not.
translations.idiomatic: Surely not.

sentences.zh: 故里人呼坊門爲宰相，謂能節宣風雨。

translations.literal: Thus townspeople call the ward gate "chancellor," saying it can regulate wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: People mock the ward gate as "chancellor" that regulates weather.

sentences.zh: 天工人代，乃爲虛設。

translations.literal: Heaven's work and man's replacement—this is vainly set.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's work is not man's to fake.

sentences.zh: 又數年以來，公私覂竭，戸口減耗，家無接新之儲，國乏俟荒之蓄。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years public and private are drained, households reduced, homes without stores of new grain, the state without reserves against famine.
translations.idiomatic: Years of drain have emptied homes and state reserves.

sentences.zh: 陛下近觀朝市，則以爲既庶且富；

translations.literal: Your Majesty lately views the markets and thinks them numerous and rich;
translations.idiomatic: You see markets and think the realm rich;

sentences.zh: 試踐閭陌，則百姓衣馬牛之衣，食犬彘之食，十室而九，丁壯盡於邊塞，孀孤轉於溝壑，猛吏奮毒，急政破資。

translations.literal: try walking the lanes—the people wear cattle and horse clothes, eat dog and pig food; nine of ten houses—stalwart men all at the frontier, widows and orphans turn in ditches; fierce officials exert poison, harsh government breaks resources.
translations.idiomatic: walk the lanes and see rags, empty homes, men at the frontier, widows in ditches, and harsh officials.

sentences.zh: 馬困斯佚，人窮斯詐。

translations.literal: Horses tired then run wild; people desperate then cheat.
translations.idiomatic: Desperation breeds crime.

sentences.zh: 起爲奸盜，從而刑之，良可嘆也。

translations.literal: They rise as bandits and are punished by law—truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: They become bandits and are punished—lamentable.

sentences.zh: 今人貧而奢不息，法設而僞不止；

translations.literal: Now people are poor yet extravagance does not cease; laws are set yet fraud does not stop;
translations.idiomatic: Poverty persists amid extravagance and fraud;

sentences.zh: 長吏貪冒，選舉以私；

translations.literal: long officials are greedy in selection through private ties;
translations.idiomatic: officials are greedy and appointments are private;

sentences.zh: 稼穡之人少，商旅之人眾。

translations.literal: few till the soil, many travel as merchants.
translations.idiomatic: farmers are few, merchants many.

sentences.zh: 願坦然更化，以身先之。

translations.literal: I wish open reform with Your Majesty first in example.
translations.idiomatic: Reform openly and lead by example.

sentences.zh: 凋殘之後，緩其力役；

translations.literal: After devastation, ease corvée;
translations.idiomatic: After devastation, ease labor;

sentences.zh: 久弊之極，訓以敦龐。

translations.literal: after long abuse, teach generous simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: after long abuse, teach thrift.

sentences.zh: 十年之外，生聚方足。

translations.literal: Beyond ten years, population will be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years population will recover.

sentences.zh: 臣聞太子者，君之貳，國之本，所以守器承祧，養民贊業。

translations.literal: I hear the crown prince is the ruler's second body, the state's root, guarding the vessel and continuing the line, nurturing the people and aiding enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the state's root—guard the succession and nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 願擇賢能，早建儲副，安社稷，慰黎元。

translations.literal: I wish to choose the worthy and able and early establish the heir to settle the altars and comfort the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a worthy heir early to secure the state.

sentences.zh: 姻戚之間，謗議所集，積疑成患，憑寵生災，愛之適以害之也。

translations.literal: Among affinal kin slander gathers; accumulated suspicion becomes illness; relying on favor breeds disaster—loving them just harms them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin breed suspicion and disaster—favor can harm.

sentences.zh: 如武三思等，誠不宜任以機要，國家利器，庸可久假於人？

translations.literal: Men like Wu Sansi truly should not be entrusted with vital affairs—the state's sharp tools, how can they be long lent to others?
translations.idiomatic: Do not entrust Wu Sansi with state power.

sentences.zh: 秘書監鄭普思、國子祭酒葉靜能挾小道淺術，列硃紫，取銀黃，虧國經，悖天道。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zheng Pusi and Directorate of Education head Ye Jingneng clutch petty arts, rank in purple, take gold seals, harm state constants, and oppose Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi and Jingneng use petty arts, take high rank, and harm the state.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「制治於未亂，保邦於未危。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Order rule before disorder, secure the state before danger.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: order rule before disorder.

sentences.zh: 此誠治亂安危之秋也。

translations.literal: This is truly the season of order, disorder, safety, and danger.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour of safety or ruin.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遠佞人，親有德，乳保之母、妃主之家，以時接見，無令媟黷。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to keep distant flatterers and be close to the virtuous; wet-nurse mothers and consorts' households—receive them in season, do not let them be profaned.
translations.idiomatic: Keep flatterers far, the virtuous near; regulate access to the inner court.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 俄以監察御史巡察河南道。

translations.literal: Soon as investigating censor he toured Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inspected Henan as censor.

sentences.zh: 時滑州輸丁少而封戸多，每配封人，皆亡命失業。

translations.literal: At the time Huazhou delivered few corvée men while fief households were many; each assignment of fief people were fugitives who lost livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou had few corvée men but many fief households who fled service.

sentences.zh: 務光建言：「通邑大都不以封。

translations.literal: Wuguang proposed: "Thoroughfare cities and great capitals should not be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Great cities should not be fiefs.

sentences.zh: 今命侯之家專擇雄奧，滑州七縣，而分封者五，王賦少於侯租，入家倍於輸國。

translations.literal: Now noble houses choose the richest lands; of Huazhou's seven counties five were enfeoffed; royal tax was less than marquis rent; income to houses doubled what entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fiefs seized Huazhou's richest counties; nobles took more than the state.

sentences.zh: 請以封戸均餘州。」

translations.literal: I ask that fief households be averaged among remaining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Spread fief households across other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又請「食賦附租庸歳送，停封使，息傳驛之勞」。

translations.literal: He also asked that "food levies attach to the annual grain tax and be sent yearly, stopping fief envoys and resting relay labor."
translations.idiomatic: Attach fief levies to regular tax and end fief envoys."

sentences.zh: 不見納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: It was rejected.

sentences.zh: 以考最，進殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: By excellent evaluation he advanced to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant censor on merit.

sentences.zh: 遷右臺。

translations.literal: Moved to the right bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the right censor bureau.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦汝州參軍事李欽憲，後爲名臣。

translations.literal: He once recommended Luoyang military adjutant Li Qinxian, who later became a famed minister.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Li Qinxian, later a famed minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: He died at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 時又有清源尉呂元泰，亦上書言時政曰：「國家者，至公之神器，一正則難傾，一傾則難正。

translations.literal: At the time Qingyuan assistant magistrate Lü Yuantai also submitted on current government saying: "The state is the vessel of utmost fairness—one rectification and it is hard to topple; one tilt and hard to right.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuantai also wrote: the state is the vessel of fairness—one error topples it.

sentences.zh: 今中興政化之始，幾微之際，可不慎哉？

translations.literal: At the beginning of restoration government, in the subtle moment—can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: At restoration's start, be cautious.

sentences.zh: 自頃營寺塔，度僧尼，施與不絶，非所謂急務也。

translations.literal: Recently building temples and towers, ordaining monks and nuns, gifts unceasing—these are not urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Temples and ordinations are not urgent.

sentences.zh: 林胡數叛，獯虜內侵，帑藏虛竭，戸口亡散。

translations.literal: Forest barbarians rebel repeatedly, steppe tribes invade within; treasuries are empty, households scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels and invaders drain the treasury; people scatter.

sentences.zh: 天下人失業，不謂太平；

translations.literal: The realm's people lose livelihood—not called peace;
translations.idiomatic: People lack livelihood—this is not peace;

sentences.zh: 邊兵未解，不謂無事；

translations.literal: frontier troops not released—not called without affairs;
translations.idiomatic: troops are not demobilized—this is not peace;

sentences.zh: 水旱爲災，不謂年登；

translations.literal: flood and drought as disaster—not called harvest;
translations.idiomatic: flood and drought persist—this is not abundance;

sentences.zh: 倉廩未實，不謂國富。

translations.literal: granaries not full—not called national wealth.
translations.idiomatic: granaries are empty—this is not wealth.

sentences.zh: 而乃驅役饑凍，雕鐫木石，營構不急，勞費日深，恐非陛下中興之要也。

translations.literal: Yet you drive the hungry and cold, carve wood and stone, construct what is not urgent—daily labor and expense deepen—I fear this is not Your Majesty's restoration imperative.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you drive the hungry to build temples—this is not restoration.

sentences.zh: 比見坊邑相率爲渾脫隊，駿馬胡服，名曰『蘇莫遮』。

translations.literal: Recently wards and towns form teams called "Sogdian fleece," fine horses and barbarian dress, named "Sumozhe."
translations.idiomatic: Wards form "Sogdian fleece" teams in barbarian dress called Sumozhe.

sentences.zh: 旗鼓相當，軍陣勢也；

translations.literal: Banners and drums oppose each other—this is army formation;
translations.idiomatic: Banners and drums mimic battle;

sentences.zh: 騰逐喧噪，戰爭象也；

translations.literal: galloping and noisy chase—this is war's image;
translations.idiomatic: noisy galloping mimics war;

sentences.zh: 錦繡誇競，害女工也；

translations.literal: brocade competition harms women's work;
translations.idiomatic: brocade wastes women's labor;

sentences.zh: 督斂貧弱，傷政體也，胡服相歡，非雅樂也；

translations.literal: pressing levies on the poor injures government; barbarian dress in mutual joy is not elegant music;
translations.idiomatic: levies on the poor injure government; barbarian dress is not court music;

sentences.zh: 渾脫爲號，非美名也。

translations.literal: "Sogdian fleece" as name is not a beautiful title.
translations.idiomatic: the name itself is ugly.

sentences.zh: 安可以禮義之朝，法胡虜之俗？

translations.literal: How can a court of ritual and righteousness take barbarian custom as law?
translations.idiomatic: How can a ritual court imitate barbarians?

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『京邑翼翼，四方是則。』

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says: 'The capital stands in majesty, and the four quarters take it as model.'
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Songs says: 'The capital stands grand, and the four quarters take their cue from it.'

sentences.zh: 非先王之禮樂而示則於四方，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: It is not the ritual and music of the former kings yet displayed as model to the four quarters—I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: To hold up non-classical ritual as a model for the empire—I cannot fathom it.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『謀，時寒若。』

translations.literal: The 《Book of Documents》 says: 'Plan as you would for severe cold.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'Plan as you would against bitter cold.'

sentences.zh: 何必臝形體，灌衢路，鼓舞跳躍而索寒焉？」

translations.literal: Why must one strip the body naked, pour water on the public roads, and drum and leap to beg for cold?
translations.idiomatic: Must one go naked, drench the streets, and dance to ward off the cold?

sentences.zh: 書聞不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was received but no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 辛替否，字協時，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou, courtesy name Xieshi, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou, styled Xieshi, was from Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 景龍中爲左拾遺。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時置公主府官屬，而安樂府補授尤濫；

translations.literal: At the time offices were set up for princess households, and appointments in the household of Princess Anle were especially indiscriminate;
translations.idiomatic: Princess households were being staffed with officials, and Princess Anle's appointments were the most reckless;

sentences.zh: 武崇訓死，主棄故宅，別築第，侈費過度；

translations.literal: When Wu Chongxun died, the princess abandoned her old residence and built a separate mansion at excessive cost;
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Chongxun's death the princess abandoned her old house and built a new mansion at ruinous expense;

sentences.zh: 又盛興佛寺，公私廢匱。

translations.literal: Buddhist temples were also built on a grand scale, and public and private resources were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist construction flourished as well, draining both public and private coffers.

sentences.zh: 替否上疏曰：

translations.literal: Tifou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou memorialized the throne:

sentences.zh: 古語曰：「福生有基，禍生有胎。」

translations.literal: An old saying runs: 'Fortune has its foundation; calamity has its womb.
translations.idiomatic: An old saying has it: 'Blessing grows from a root; disaster from a seed.

sentences.zh: 且公主，陛下愛子也，選賢嫁之，設官輔之，傾府庫以賜之，壯第觀以居之，廣池御以嬉之，可謂至重至憐也。

translations.literal: Moreover the princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter: you chose a worthy man to marry her, set up officials to assist her, emptied the treasury to endow her, built grand mansions and pavilions for her dwelling, and broad ponds and gardens for her pleasure—this may be called utmost honor and utmost affection.
translations.idiomatic: Your daughter has been given a worthy husband, a staff of officials, gifts from the treasury, a splendid residence, and gardens for her delight—nothing could show more honor and love.

sentences.zh: 然用不合古義，行不根人心，將變愛成憎，轉福爲禍。

translations.literal: Yet the use does not accord with ancient principle, and the conduct is not rooted in the people's hearts; love will turn to hatred and fortune to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these measures violate ancient norms and alienate the people; affection will become hatred and blessing become curse.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 竭人之力，費人之財，奪人之家，怨也。

translations.literal: To exhaust men's strength, spend men's wealth, and seize men's homes is to breed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Draining labor, spending wealth, and seizing homes breeds resentment.

sentences.zh: 愛一女，取三怨於天下，使邊疆士不盡力，朝廷士不盡忠。

translations.literal: To love one daughter and incur three resentments under Heaven is to make frontier soldiers not exert themselves fully and court officials not serve loyally.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring one daughter wins three hatreds across the realm: frontier troops withhold their strength and court officials withhold their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 人心散矣，獨持所愛，何所恃乎？

translations.literal: When hearts are scattered, what can one rely on by clinging to a single beloved?
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are divided, on what can Your Majesty rely by clinging to one favorite?

sentences.zh: 向使魯王賞同諸婿，則有今日之福，無曩日之禍。

translations.literal: If in the past Prince of Lu had been rewarded like other sons-in-law, there would be today's fortune without yesterday's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Had the Prince of Lu been treated like other imperial sons-in-law, today's blessings would never have become yesterday's disaster.

sentences.zh: 人徒見其禍，不知禍所來，所以禍者，寵過也。

translations.literal: People only see the calamity and do not know whence it came; the cause of calamity is excessive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Men see the ruin but not its source: calamity comes from excessive indulgence.

sentences.zh: 今棄一宅，造一宅，忘前悔，忽後禍，臣竊謂陛下乃憎之，非愛之也。

translations.literal: Now one mansion is abandoned and another built; past regret is forgotten and future calamity ignored—I privately think Your Majesty in fact hates her, not loves her.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning one mansion to build another, forgetting past regret and ignoring future ruin—I fear Your Majesty hates her rather than loves her.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君以人爲本，本固則邦寧，邦寧則陛下夫婦母子長相保也。

translations.literal: I have heard that the ruler takes the people as foundation; when the foundation is firm the state is secure, and when the state is secure Your Majesty's consort, children, and mother may long preserve one another.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's foundation is the people; when that foundation is firm the realm is secure, and then Your Majesty's family may endure.

sentences.zh: 願外謀宰臣，爲久安計，不使奸臣賊子有以伺之。

translations.literal: I wish you would consult chief ministers outside for a plan of lasting peace, and not let treacherous ministers and wicked sons find openings to watch for.
translations.idiomatic: Consult your chief ministers on a plan for lasting peace, lest traitors and schemers find their chance.

sentences.zh: 今疆場危駭，倉廩空虛，卒輸不充，士賞不及，而大建寺宇，廣造第宅。

translations.literal: Now the frontiers are perilous and alarmed, granaries empty, transport of supplies insufficient, and soldiers' rewards unpaid, yet temples are built on a grand scale and mansions widely constructed.
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers are in peril, granaries empty, supplies unpaid, and soldiers unrewarded—yet temples and mansions rise everywhere.

sentences.zh: 伐木空山，不給棟梁；

translations.literal: Timber is cut from empty mountains yet cannot supply beams and rafters;
translations.idiomatic: Mountains are stripped of timber yet cannot supply a single beam;

sentences.zh: 運土塞路，不充墻壁。

translations.literal: earth is moved to block roads yet cannot fill a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is hauled to choke the roads yet cannot fill one wall.

sentences.zh: 所謂佛者，清凈慈悲，體道以濟物，不欲利以損人，不榮身以害教。

translations.literal: What is called Buddha is pure, compassionate, embodying the Way to aid beings, unwilling to profit at others' loss or glorify the body to harm the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha means purity and compassion, embodying the Way to help others—not profiting at men's expense or glorifying oneself at the teaching's cost.

sentences.zh: 今三時之月，掘山穿地，損命也；

translations.literal: Now in the months of the three seasons mountains are dug and earth pierced—this harms life;
translations.idiomatic: In the growing season mountains are dug and earth torn up—this destroys life;

sentences.zh: 殫府虛帑，損人也；

translations.literal: treasuries are emptied—this harms the people;
translations.idiomatic: treasuries are drained—this harms the people;

sentences.zh: 廣殿長廊，榮身也。

translations.literal: vast halls and long corridors glorify the body.
translations.idiomatic: vast halls and corridors glorify the self.

sentences.zh: 損命則不慈悲，損人則不愛物，榮身則不清凈，寧佛者之心乎？

translations.literal: To harm life is not compassion; to harm people is not love of beings; to glorify the body is not purity—is this the mind of Buddha?
translations.idiomatic: Destroying life is not compassion, harming people is not love, self-glorification is not purity—is this the Buddha's way?

sentences.zh: 昔夏爲天子，二十餘世而商受之，商二十餘世而周受之，周三十餘世而漢受之，由漢而後，歷代可知已。

translations.literal: Formerly Xia ruled as Son of Heaven for more than twenty generations before Shang received the mandate; Shang for more than twenty before Zhou; Zhou for more than thirty before Han; from Han onward the succession of dynasties is known.
translations.idiomatic: Xia held the throne for twenty-odd generations before Shang took it; Shang for twenty-odd before Zhou; Zhou for thirty-odd before Han—and the dynasties since Han are known.

sentences.zh: 咸有道之長，無道之短，豈窮金玉修塔廟享久長之祚乎？

translations.literal: All had long reigns when there was the Way and short when there was not—can exhausting gold and jade to build pagodas and temples secure long-lasting fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous rule endured; vicious rule did not—can piling gold and jade into temples secure a lasting throne?

sentences.zh: 臣以爲減雕琢之費以周不足，是有佛之德；

translations.literal: I think that to reduce carving and ornament to relieve want is to have Buddha's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Cutting ornament to relieve want would be Buddha's virtue;

sentences.zh: 息穿掘之苦以全昆蟲，是有佛之仁；

translations.literal: to cease digging and piercing to preserve insects is to have Buddha's benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: ending excavation to spare even insects would be Buddha's benevolence;

sentences.zh: 罷營構之直以給邊垂，是有湯、武之功；

translations.literal: to stop construction costs and supply the frontiers is to have the achievement of Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: halting construction to fund the frontiers would be the achievement of Tang and Wu;

sentences.zh: 回不急之祿以購廉清，是有唐、虞之治。

translations.literal: to redirect unneeded stipends to reward integrity and purity is to have the governance of Tang of Yu and Yu of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: redirecting needless salaries to reward honest officials would be the governance of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 陛下緩其所急，急其所緩，親未來，疏見在，失真實，冀虛無，重俗人之所爲，而輕天子之業，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is slow where urgency is needed and urgent where slowness is needed; you cherish what is not yet come and neglect what is present; you lose what is real and hope for what is empty; you value what vulgar men do and slight the Son of Heaven's task—I am pained at this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty neglects what is urgent and rushes what can wait, cherishing the unseen and slighting the present, chasing emptiness and undervaluing the imperial charge—I am deeply pained.

sentences.zh: 今出財依勢，避役亡命，類度爲沙門，其未度者，窮民善人耳。

translations.literal: Now those who pay out wealth rely on power; those evading corvée flee as outlaws; many are tonsured as monks, while those not tonsured are only poor people and good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth buys tonsure, power evades labor, and only the poor and honest remain laymen.

sentences.zh: 拔親樹知，豈離朋黨，畜妻養孥，非無私愛，是致人毀道，非廣道求人也。

translations.literal: Promoting kin and planting favorites—can this be apart from faction? Keeping wives and raising children is not without private affection; this makes men ruin the Way—it is not spreading the Way to seek people.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring kin and cronies is faction; keeping wives and children shows private attachment—this defiles the teaching rather than spreading it.

sentences.zh: 陛下常欲填池塹，捐苑囿，以賑貧人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has often wished to fill ponds and ditches and give up parks and preserves to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has often spoken of filling ponds and giving up parks to aid the poor.

sentences.zh: 今天下之寺無數，一寺當陛下一宮，壯麗用度尚或過之。

translations.literal: Now temples under Heaven are countless; one temple equals one of Your Majesty's palaces, and in splendor and expense may even surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Temples now number beyond count; each rivals a palace in splendor and expense.

sentences.zh: 十分天下之財而佛有七八，陛下何有之矣？

translations.literal: Seven or eight tenths of the wealth under Heaven belong to Buddhism—what does Your Majesty still possess?
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight parts in ten of the realm's wealth belong to Buddhism—what remains for the throne?

sentences.zh: 雖役不食之人、不衣之士，猶尚不給，況必待天生地養、風動雨潤而後得之乎？

translations.literal: Even if one conscripted men who do not eat and scholars who do not wear clothes, it would still not suffice—how much less when one must wait for Heaven's birth and Earth's nurture, wind's stirring and rain's moistening, to obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Even conscripting men who need no food or clothing would not suffice—how much less when wealth must wait on rain and harvest?

sentences.zh: 臣聞國無九年之儲，曰非其國。

translations.literal: I have heard that a state without nine years' stores is called no true state.
translations.idiomatic: A state without nine years' grain reserves is no true state.

sentences.zh: 今計倉廩，度府庫，百僚共給，萬事用度，臣恐不能卒歳。

translations.literal: Now reckoning granaries and estimating treasuries, with all officials supplied and every expense met, I fear we cannot last out the year.
translations.idiomatic: Reckoning granaries and treasuries against every official's salary and every expense, I fear the year cannot be finished.

sentences.zh: 假如兵旱相乘，則沙門不能擐甲胄，寺塔不足穰饑饉矣。

translations.literal: If war and drought should come together, monks cannot don armor and temples and pagodas cannot relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: If war and drought strike together, monks cannot bear arms and temples cannot feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，罷斜封官千餘人，俄詔復之。

translations.literal: When Ruizong acceded, more than a thousand irregularly appointed officials were dismissed, but soon an edict restored them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne he dismissed over a thousand irregular appointees, but soon restored them by edict.

sentences.zh: 方營金仙、玉真觀。

translations.literal: He was just then building the Golden Immortal and Jade True abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: He was then building the Golden Immortal and Jade True abbeys.

sentences.zh: 替否以左補闕上疏曰：

translations.literal: Tifou, as Left Supplementation Censor, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou, now Left Supplementation Censor, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣謂古之用度不時、爵賞不當、國破家亡者，口説不若身逢，耳聞不若目見，臣請以有唐治道得失，陛下所及見者言之。

translations.literal: I say that in antiquity those whose expenditures were untimely and rewards improper brought ruin on state and family—words are not like experiencing it oneself, hearing is not like seeing with one's eyes; I ask to speak of the gains and losses of Tang governance from what Your Majesty has witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient states fell when spending was ill-timed and rewards unjust—hearing is not seeing. Let me speak of Tang's successes and failures from what Your Majesty has witnessed.

sentences.zh: 太宗，陛下之祖，撥亂立極，得至治之體。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, Your Majesty's ancestor, quelled disorder and established the supreme norm, attaining the substance of perfect governance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, your ancestor, quelled chaos and established perfect governance.

sentences.zh: 省官清吏，舉天下職司無虛授，用天下財帛無枉費；

translations.literal: He reduced offices and purified officials; throughout the realm no post was given in vain and no wealth wasted;
translations.idiomatic: He trimmed offices, purified the bureaucracy, wasted no appointment and misspent no coin;

sentences.zh: 賞必待功，官必得才，爲無不成，征無不服。

translations.literal: rewards awaited merit, offices awaited talent; undertakings did not fail and campaigns did not go unsubdued.
translations.idiomatic: rewards followed merit, offices went to talent; every task succeeded and every campaign prevailed.

sentences.zh: 不多寺觀而福祿至，不度僧尼而咎殃滅。

translations.literal: Without many temples and abbeys, fortune and emolument came; without tonsuring monks and nuns, blame and calamity vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Without lavish temples, fortune came; without mass tonsures, calamity faded.

sentences.zh: 陰陽不愆，五穀遂成，粟腐帛爛。

translations.literal: Yin and yang were not out of balance; the five grains flourished; grain rotted from abundance and silk from excess.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth were in harmony, harvests abundant, grain and silk piled in surplus.

sentences.zh: 萬里貢賦，百蠻歸款。

translations.literal: Tribute came from ten thousand li; the hundred barbarians submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute flowed from afar and barbarian peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 享國久長，多歷年所。

translations.literal: He enjoyed the state long, through many years.
translations.idiomatic: His reign endured for many years.

sentences.zh: 陛下何憚而不法之？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty hesitate and not take him as model?
translations.idiomatic: Why hesitate to follow his example?

sentences.zh: 中宗，陛下之兄，居先帝之業，忽先帝之化，不聽賢臣之言，而悅子女之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, Your Majesty's elder brother, occupied the former emperor's enterprise yet neglected the former emperor's transformation; he did not heed worthy ministers but indulged his children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, your brother, inherited the throne but abandoned his father's reforms, heeding flatterers rather than worthy ministers and indulging his children.

sentences.zh: 虛食祿者數千人，妄食士者百餘戸；

translations.literal: Thousands ate salaries in vain; more than a hundred households ate stipends without warrant;
translations.idiomatic: Thousands drew salaries without work; hundreds of households received stipends without cause;

sentences.zh: 造寺蠹財數百億，度人免租、庸數十萬。

translations.literal: building temples devoured hundreds of millions; tonsuring people exempted hundreds of thousands from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: temples consumed hundreds of millions; tonsures exempted hundreds of thousands from tax and labor.

sentences.zh: 是故國家所出日加，所入日減，倉乏半歳之儲，庫無一時之帛。

translations.literal: Thus state expenditure daily increased and income daily decreased; granaries lacked half a year's stores and treasuries not a moment's silk.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure rose daily while revenue fell; granaries held less than half a year and treasuries not a day's silk.

sentences.zh: 所惡者逐，逐必忠良；

translations.literal: Those he hated were driven out, and those driven out were surely the loyal and good;
translations.idiomatic: Those he hated were expelled—and the expelled were the loyal;

sentences.zh: 所愛者賞，賞皆讒慝。

translations.literal: those he loved were rewarded, and those rewarded were all slanderers and villains.
translations.idiomatic: those he favored were rewarded—and the rewarded were slanderers.

sentences.zh: 朋佞喋喋，交相傾動。

translations.literal: Factions of flatterers chattered endlessly and mutually undermined one another.
translations.idiomatic: Factions of flatterers schemed and undermined one another.

sentences.zh: 奪百姓之食以養殘兇，剝萬人之衣以塗土木。

translations.literal: He seized the people's food to nourish the cruel and violent and stripped ten thousand men's garments to plaster wood and earth.
translations.idiomatic: He took the people's food to feed villains and stripped their clothes to gild temples.

sentences.zh: 人怨神怒，親忿眾離，水旱疾疫，六年之間，三禍爲變。

translations.literal: Men resented, spirits were angered, kin were enraged and the multitude scattered; flood, drought, and pestilence—in six years three calamities transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Men resented, spirits raged, kin turned away; in six years flood, drought, and pestilence struck.

sentences.zh: 享國不永，受終於兇婦，取譏萬代，詒笑四夷，陛下所見也。

translations.literal: He did not long enjoy the state and met his end at a vicious woman's hands, drawing mockery for ten thousand generations and laughter from the four barbarians—Your Majesty has seen this.
translations.idiomatic: His reign was brief and ended at a wicked woman's hands—a scandal for all time and mockery among barbarians, as Your Majesty knows.

sentences.zh: 若法太宗治國，太山之安可致也；

translations.literal: If one modeled Taizong's governance, Mount Tai's security could be attained;
translations.idiomatic: Follow Taizong and the realm will stand firm as Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 法中宗治國，累卵之危亦可致也。

translations.literal: model Zhongzong's governance and the peril of piled eggs could also be attained.
translations.idiomatic: follow Zhongzong and the realm will totter like a pile of eggs.

sentences.zh: 頃淫雨不解，穀荒於壟，麥爛於場，入秋亢旱，霜損蟲暴，草木枯黃，下人咨嗟，未知所濟。

translations.literal: Recently unceasing heavy rain left grain wasted in the fields and wheat rotted on the threshing floor; entering autumn severe drought came, frost damaged crops and insects swarmed; grass and trees withered yellow; common people lamented, not knowing how to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains ruined the fields, wheat rotted in the stacks; then drought, frost, and pests withered the crops, and the people despaired with no relief in sight.

sentences.zh: 而營寺造觀，日繼於時，道路流言，計用緡錢百餘萬。

translations.literal: Yet building temples and abbeys continued day after day; rumor on the roads estimated the cost at more than a million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yet temple construction goes on daily, rumor putting the cost at over a million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 陛下知倉有幾歳儲？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty know how many years' stores the granaries hold?
translations.idiomatic: How many years' grain do the granaries hold?

sentences.zh: 庫有幾歳帛？

translations.literal: How many years' silk do the treasuries hold?
translations.idiomatic: How many years' silk do the treasuries hold?

sentences.zh: 百姓何所活？

translations.literal: How are the common people to live?
translations.idiomatic: How are the people to survive?

sentences.zh: 三邊何所輸？

translations.literal: What will the three frontiers be supplied with?
translations.idiomatic: What will supply the frontiers?

sentences.zh: 民散兵亂，職此由也。

translations.literal: The scattering of the people and disorder of troops—this is where the cause lies.
translations.idiomatic: Popular unrest and military disorder stem from this.

sentences.zh: 而以百萬構無用之觀，受天下之怨。

translations.literal: Yet with a million one builds useless abbeys and incurs resentment under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a million is spent on useless abbeys, earning the realm's hatred.

sentences.zh: 陛下忍棄太宗之治本，不忍棄中宗之亂階；

translations.literal: Your Majesty can bear to abandon Taizong's foundation of governance yet cannot bear to abandon Zhongzong's steps toward chaos;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty can abandon Taizong's foundation but not Zhongzong's path to ruin;

sentences.zh: 忍棄太宗久長之謀，不忍棄中宗短促之計。

translations.literal: can abandon Taizong's plan for long endurance yet cannot abandon Zhongzong's short-lived scheme.
translations.idiomatic: can abandon Taizong's plan for lasting rule but not Zhongzong's short-sighted schemes.

sentences.zh: 何以繼祖宗、觀萬國耶？

translations.literal: How then to continue the ancestors and face the myriad states?
translations.idiomatic: How then can you honor your ancestors or face the world?

sentences.zh: 陛下在韋氏時，切齒群兇；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was under the Wei clan, you gnashed teeth at the gang of villains;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei clan Your Majesty gnashed teeth at the villains;

sentences.zh: 今貴爲天子，不改其事，恐復有切齒於陛下者。

translations.literal: now exalted as Son of Heaven, if you do not change these affairs, I fear there will again be those who gnash teeth at Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: now enthroned, if you continue the same ways, others will gnash teeth at you in turn.

sentences.zh: 往見明敕，一用貞觀故事。

translations.literal: I have seen clear edicts that everything should follow Zhenguan precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts have declared that all should follow the Zhenguan model.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀有營寺觀，加浮屠、黃老，益無用之官，行不急之務者乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, in Zhenguan were temples and abbeys built, Buddhist and Daoist added, useless offices increased, and non-urgent tasks pursued?
translations.idiomatic: Did the Zhenguan era build temples, add Buddhist and Daoist offices, and pursue non-urgent tasks?

sentences.zh: 往者和帝之憐悖逆也，宗晉卿勸爲第宅，趙履溫勸爲園亭，工徒未息，義兵交馳，亭不得游，宅不得息，信邪僻之説，成骨肉之刑，陛下所見也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor He pitied the rebellious, Zong Jinqing urged building mansions and Zhao Lüwen urged building gardens and pavilions; workers had not ceased when righteous troops clashed; pavilions could not be enjoyed and mansions could not be rested in; believing perverse doctrines brought kin punishment by law—Your Majesty has seen this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He indulged rebels, Zong Jinqing urged mansions and Zhao Lüwen urged gardens; before construction ended, loyal troops clashed; believing evil counsel brought kin to the executioner's block—as Your Majesty witnessed.

sentences.zh: 今茲二觀，得無晉卿之徒陰勸爲之，冀娛骨肉？

translations.literal: These two abbeys now—are they not urged in secret by men like Jinqing, hoping to amuse kin?
translations.idiomatic: Are these two abbeys not urged in secret by men like Jinqing, hoping to distract the imperial family?

sentences.zh: 不可不察也。

translations.literal: This cannot but be examined.
translations.idiomatic: This must be investigated.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下停二觀以須豐年，以所費之財給貧窮、填府庫，則公主福無窮矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty stops the two abbeys to await a bountiful year and uses the funds to aid the poor and fill the treasuries will the princess's fortune be endless.
translations.idiomatic: Stop the two abbeys until harvest is rich, give the funds to the poor and fill the treasuries, and the princess's blessing will be endless.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝不能用，然嘉切直。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor could not adopt it, yet he praised its blunt honesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not adopt the memorial but praised its blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Palace Censor of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Palace Censor on the Right.

sentences.zh: 雍令劉少微恃權貪贓，替否按之，岑羲屢以爲請，替否曰：「我爲憲司，懼勢以縱罪，謂王法何？」

translations.literal: Liu Shaowei, magistrate of Yong, relied on power and was greedy and corrupt; Tifou investigated him; Cen Yi repeatedly interceded; Tifou said: "I serve the censorate—if I fear power and release guilt, what becomes of royal law?
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Liu Shaowei of Yong abused power and took bribes; Tifou investigated him. Cen Yi repeatedly interceded. Tifou said: "As censor, if I fear power and release the guilty, what becomes of the law?

sentences.zh: 少微坐死。

translations.literal: Shaowei was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was executed.

sentences.zh: 遷累潁王府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred and eventually became chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually made chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 李渤，字浚之，魏橫野將軍、申國公發之裔。

translations.literal: Li Bo, courtesy name Junzhi, was a descendant of Li Fa, General of Hengye and Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo, styled Junzhi, was descended from Li Fa, General of Hengye and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，殿中侍御史，以不能養母廢於世。

translations.literal: His father Jun was a Palace Censor and was cast out from society for failing to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun, a Palace Censor, was disgraced for failing to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 渤恥之，不肯仕，刻志於學，與仲兄涉偕隱廬山。

translations.literal: Bo was shamed by this, refused office, devoted himself zealously to learning, and with his elder brother She retired together to Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was shamed by this, refused office, devoted himself to study, and retired to Mount Lu with his elder brother She.

sentences.zh: 嘗以列禦寇拒粟，其妻怒，是無婦也；

translations.literal: Once when Lie Yukou refused grain, his wife grew angry—this showed he was no proper husband;
translations.idiomatic: When Lie Yukou once refused grain, his wife rebuked him—such a man was no husband;

sentences.zh: 樂羊子舍金，妻讓之，是無夫也。

translations.literal: when Leyangzi abandoned gold, his wife reproached him—this showed he was no proper husband.
translations.idiomatic: when Leyangzi abandoned gold, his wife scolded him—such a man was no husband.

sentences.zh: 乃摭古聯德高蹈者，以楚接輿、老萊子、黔婁先生、於陵子、王孺仲、梁鴻六人，圖象贊其行，因以自儆。

translations.literal: He then gathered ancient men of linked virtue and lofty withdrawal—Chu Jieyu, Old Master Lai, Master Qianlou, the Lord of Yuling, Wang Ruzhong, and Liang Hong, six men—and made portraits praising their conduct, thereby admonishing himself.
translations.idiomatic: He collected six ancient recluses of noble character—Jieyu of Chu, Old Master Lai, Master Qianlou, the Lord of Yuling, Wang Ruzhong, and Liang Hong—portrayed and praised them as a warning to himself.

sentences.zh: 久之，更徙少室。

translations.literal: After a long time he moved again to Lesser Chamber Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he moved to Lesser Chamber Mountain.

sentences.zh: 元和初，戸部侍郎李巽、諫議大夫韋況交章薦之，詔以右拾遺召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Vice Minister of Revenue Li Xun and Remonstrance Grandee Wei Kuang jointly recommended him in memorials, and an edict summoned him as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe, Li Xun and Wei Kuang jointly recommended him, and he was summoned as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 於是河南少尹杜兼遣吏持詔、幣即山敦促，渤上書謝：「昔屠羊説有言：『位三旌，祿萬鐘，知貴於屠羊，然不可使吾君妄施。』

translations.literal: Thereupon Henan Vice Prefect Du Jian sent an official with the edict and gifts to the mountain to urge him; Bo submitted a letter declining: "Formerly Tuyang Shuo said: 'Rank of three banners and salary of ten thousand piculs—I know this is nobler than butchering sheep, yet one must not let our lord bestow rewards rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Vice Prefect Du Jian sent an envoy with edict and gifts to urge him from the mountain. Bo wrote declining: "Tuyang Shuo once said: 'Three banners and ten thousand piculs—I know that outranks butchering sheep, yet one must not let the ruler bestow rewards rashly.

sentences.zh: 彼賤賈也，猶能忘己愛君。

translations.literal: That base peddler could still forget himself and love his lord.
translations.idiomatic: That humble peddler could still forget himself for his lord's sake.

sentences.zh: 臣雖欲盜榮以濟所欲，得無愧屠羊乎？」

translations.literal: Though I wish to steal honor to satisfy my desires, would I not be ashamed before the sheep-butcher?
translations.idiomatic: If I seized honor to satisfy my desires, would I not be ashamed before Tuyang Shuo?

sentences.zh: 不拜。

translations.literal: He did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令韓愈遺書曰：

translations.literal: Luoyang Magistrate Han Yu sent a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang Magistrate Han Yu wrote to him:

sentences.zh: 有詔河南敦喻拾遺公，朝廷士引頸東望，若景星、鳳鳥始見，爭先睹之爲快。

translations.literal: An edict has ordered Henan to earnestly persuade the Reminder; court gentlemen stretch their necks eastward as when the auspicious star or phoenix first appears, vying to see him first for joy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict has ordered Henan to persuade you to serve; court gentlemen crane their necks eastward as at the first sight of an auspicious star or phoenix, eager to see you.

sentences.zh: 方今天子仁聖，大小之事皆出宰相，樂善言如不得聞，自即大位，凡所出而施者無不得宜。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is benevolent and sage; great and small affairs all come from the chief ministers; he delights in good counsel as if he could not hear enough; since taking the throne, nothing he has issued and enacted has been inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is benevolent and sage; affairs great and small rest with the chief ministers; he thirsts for good counsel; since his accession nothing he has done has been amiss.

sentences.zh: 勤儉之聲，寬大之政，幽閨婦女、草野小子飽聞而厭道之。

translations.literal: Reports of diligence and frugality, policies of generosity and breadth—women in inner chambers and lads in the wilds are sated with hearing and weary of speaking of them.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality and magnanimity are on every tongue—even women at home and boys in the fields speak of them until weary.

sentences.zh: 愈不通於古，請問先生，茲非太平世歟？

translations.literal: Yu is not versed in antiquity and asks the master: is this not an age of great peace?
translations.idiomatic: I am no scholar of antiquity, but tell me, sir—is this not an age of great peace?

sentences.zh: 加又有非人力而至者，年穀屢熟，符貺委至。

translations.literal: Moreover there are things not achieved by human effort: harvests repeatedly abundant, auspicious omens arriving in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover harvests abound year after year and auspicious omens arrive in succession without human effort.

sentences.zh: 干紀之奸不戰而拘累，強梁之兇銷鑠縮慄，迎風而委伏。

translations.literal: Traitors against the norm are bound without battle; violent bullies melt, shrink, and tremble, bowing before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors are seized without a fight; bullies melt and tremble, bowing before the wind.

sentences.zh: 其有一事未就正，視若不成人。

translations.literal: If one thing is not set right, it seems as if the work is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: If one thing remains unsettled, the whole achievement seems incomplete.

sentences.zh: 四海所環，無一夫甲而兵者。

translations.literal: Within the four seas that encircle us, not one man wears armor for war.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas, not a man bears arms.

sentences.zh: 若此時也，遺公不疾起與天下士樂而享之，斯無時矣。

translations.literal: At such a time, if the recluse does not swiftly rise to share and enjoy it with gentlemen under Heaven, there will never be such a time again.
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment, if you do not rise swiftly to share this joy with the empire's worthies, the moment will never return.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子知不可爲而爲之不已，跡接於諸侯之國。

translations.literal: Formerly Confucius knew it could not be done yet did not cease doing it; his tracks reached the states of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius knew the times were against him yet never ceased his work, traveling among the feudal states.

sentences.zh: 今可爲之時，自藏深山，牢關而固拒，即與仁義者異守矣。

translations.literal: Now when it can be done, to hide oneself in deep mountains, bar the gates and firmly refuse—this is to hold a different standard from men of benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now when service is possible, to hide in the mountains and firmly refuse is to depart from the way of the humane and righteous.

sentences.zh: 想遺公冠帶就車，惠然肯來，舒所畜積，以補綴盛德之闕，利加於時，名垂將來。

translations.literal: I imagine the recluse donning cap and belt and taking carriage, graciously consenting to come, unfolding what he has stored to mend the gaps in supreme virtue—benefit added to the age, fame handed down to the future.
translations.idiomatic: Imagine you don cap and belt, take carriage, and come graciously, unfolding your store of wisdom to mend what is lacking in this glorious age—benefiting the present and winning fame for the future.

sentences.zh: 踴躍懷企，頃刻以冀。

translations.literal: Leaping with joy and filled with expectation, I hope for it moment by moment.
translations.idiomatic: I leap with hope and await you every moment.

sentences.zh: 又切聞朝廷議，必起遺公，使者往若不許，即河南必繼以行。

translations.literal: I also hear urgently that the court has resolved to summon the recluse; if the envoy goes and you do not consent, Henan will surely follow with another mission.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the court has resolved to summon you; if the first envoy fails, Henan will send another.

sentences.zh: 拾遺徵若不至，更加高秩。

translations.literal: If the Reminder is summoned and does not come, an even higher rank will be added.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not come when summoned as Reminder, a higher rank will be offered.

sentences.zh: 如是辭少就多，傷於廉而害於義，遺公必不爲也。

translations.literal: Thus to decline the lesser and accept the greater injures integrity and harms righteousness—the recluse surely would not do this.
translations.idiomatic: To decline the lesser post and accept the greater would injure integrity and righteousness—you surely would not do that.

sentences.zh: 善人進其類，皆有望於公。

translations.literal: Good men advance their kind; all have hopes in you.
translations.idiomatic: Good men advance their fellows; all look to you with hope.

sentences.zh: 公不爲起，是使天子不盡得良臣，君子不盡得顯位，人庶不盡被惠利，其害不爲細。

translations.literal: If you do not rise, it makes the Son of Heaven not fully obtain good ministers, gentlemen not fully obtain prominent posts, and the people not fully receive benefits—the harm is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to serve, the emperor loses good ministers, gentlemen lose their posts, and the people lose their benefits—the harm is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 必審察而諦思之，務使合於孔子之道乃善。

translations.literal: You must examine and ponder carefully, striving to accord with the Way of Confucius—then it will be good.
translations.idiomatic: Consider carefully and strive to accord with Confucius's way—that would be best.

sentences.zh: 渤心善其言，始出家東都，每朝廷有闕政，輒附章列上。

translations.literal: Bo was pleased at heart with these words and first left the mountains for the eastern capital; whenever the court had a policy lapse he would attach a memorial listing it and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was moved by these words and left the mountains for the eastern capital; whenever he saw a policy lapse he memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 元和九年討淮西，上平賊三術：一曰感，二曰守，三曰戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe when Huai West was attacked, he submitted three methods for pacifying rebels: first persuasion, second defense, third battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 9, during the campaign against Huai West, he proposed three methods to pacify rebels: persuasion, defense, and battle.

sentences.zh: 感不成，不失爲守；

translations.literal: If persuasion fails, one still has defense;
translations.idiomatic: If persuasion fails, defense remains;

sentences.zh: 守不成，不失爲戰。

translations.literal: if defense fails, one still has battle.
translations.idiomatic: if defense fails, battle remains.

sentences.zh: 又上《御戎新錄》，乃以著作郎召，渤遂起。

translations.literal: He also submitted New Records on Governing the Frontier; then he was summoned as Compiler and Bo finally accepted office.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted New Records on Governing the Frontier and was summoned as Compiler; Bo finally accepted office.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，遷右補闕，以直忤旨，下遷丹王府諮議參軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor; for bluntness that offended the imperial will he was demoted to advisory staff of the Prince of Dan's household, serving in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made Right Supplementation Censor; his bluntness offended the throne and he was demoted to advisory staff of the Prince of Dan's household in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上言：

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 至德以來，天下思致治平，訖今不稱者，人倦而不知變。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide era the realm has sought perfect governance and peace; that it is still not so called is because men are weary and do not know to change.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era the realm has sought peace and good governance; that it is still not achieved is because men are weary and do not know how to change.

sentences.zh: 天以變通之運遺陛下，陛下順而革之，則悠久。

translations.literal: Heaven has bequeathed Your Majesty the fortune of change and adaptation; if Your Majesty follows and reforms, the reign will be enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has given Your Majesty the fortune of change; follow it and reform, and the reign will endure.

sentences.zh: 宜乘平蔡之勢，以德羈服恆、兗無不濟，則恩威暢矣。

translations.literal: You should ride the momentum of pacifying Cai and with virtue bind and subdue Heng and Yan—nothing would fail, and grace and authority would flow freely.
translations.idiomatic: Ride the momentum of pacifying Cai and with virtue win over Heng and Yan—then grace and authority will both prevail.

sentences.zh: 昔舜、禹以匹夫宅四海，其烈如彼；

translations.literal: Formerly Shun and Yu as common men possessed the four seas—their achievement was thus;
translations.idiomatic: Shun and Yu began as common men yet ruled the world—such was their achievement;

sentences.zh: 今以五聖營太平，其難如此。

translations.literal: now with five sage emperors building great peace, the difficulty is thus.
translations.idiomatic: yet with five sage emperors building peace, the difficulty is still so great.

sentences.zh: 臣恐宰相群臣蘊晦術略，啟沃有所未盡，使陛下翹然思文、武、禹、湯而不獲也。

translations.literal: I fear the chief ministers and officials conceal their strategies and in counsel do not fully expound, making Your Majesty eagerly think of Wen, Wu, Yu, and Tang yet not attain them.
translations.idiomatic: I fear ministers conceal their counsel and do not fully advise, leaving Your Majesty longing for the example of Wen, Wu, Yu, and Tang in vain.

sentences.zh: 宜正六官，敘九疇，修王制、月令，崇孝悌，敦九族，廣諫路，黜選舉，復俊造，定四民，省抑佛、老，明刑行令，治兵御戎。

translations.literal: You should rectify the six ministries, arrange the nine categories, restore royal institutions and monthly ordinances, honor filial piety and brotherly duty, strengthen the nine kin groups, broaden the path of remonstrance, reform selection and appointment, restore the recruitment of talent, fix the four classes of people, reduce and restrain Buddhism and Daoism, clarify punishments and enforce orders, and govern troops and defend the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Rectify the six ministries, restore royal institutions, honor filial piety, broaden remonstrance, reform appointments, restore talent recruitment, fix the four classes of people, restrain Buddhism and Daoism, clarify law, and govern the military.

sentences.zh: 願下宰相公卿大夫議，博引海內名儒，大開學館，與群臣參講，據經稽古、應時便俗者，使切磋周復，作制度，合宣父繼周之言。

translations.literal: I wish you would send the matter down to chief ministers, grandees, and grand masters for discussion, broadly invite famous Confucians within the seas, greatly open academies, and with officials jointly lecture—those who base themselves on the classics, examine antiquity, and suit the times and customs—making them refine one another in full circuit and establish institutions conforming to the Master continuing Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Send the matter to ministers and grandees for debate, invite renowned scholars, open academies, and with officials jointly study the classics to establish institutions worthy of Confucius's vision of continuing the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 謹上五事：一禮樂，二食貨，三刑政，四議都，五辨讎。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit five matters: first ritual and music, second food and wealth, third punishments and government, fourth discussion of the capital, fifth distinguishing enmity.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit five topics: ritual and music, food and wealth, punishments and government, the capital, and distinguishing enmity.

sentences.zh: 渤雖處外，然志存朝廷，表疏凡四十五獻。

translations.literal: Though Bo was posted outside, his mind remained with the court; memorials totaled forty-five submissions.
translations.idiomatic: Though posted outside the capital, Bo's heart remained with the court; he submitted forty-five memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 擢爲庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Storehouse Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Storehouse Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會皇甫鎛輔政，務剝下佐用度，而渤奉詔吊郗士美喪，在道上言：「渭南長源鄕戸四百，今才四十；

translations.literal: When Huangfu Bo assisted in government and strove to squeeze the people to supplement expenditures, Bo was on mission by edict to mourn Xi Shimei's death and on the road submitted: "In Changyuan township of Weinan there were four hundred households; now there are only forty;
translations.idiomatic: When Huangfu Bo governed and squeezed the people to fill the treasury, Bo was traveling on imperial business to mourn Xi Shimei and wrote: "Changyuan township in Weinan had four hundred households; now there are forty;

sentences.zh: 閿鄕戸三千，而今千。

translations.literal: In Min township there were three thousand households; now one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Min township had three thousand; now one thousand.

sentences.zh: 它州縣大抵類此。

translations.literal: Other prefectures and counties are mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Other prefectures and counties are much the same.

sentences.zh: 推其敝，始於攤逃人之賦。

translations.literal: Tracing the harm, it began with spreading fugitives' taxes onto others.
translations.idiomatic: The root of the evil is spreading fugitives' tax burdens onto those who remain.

sentences.zh: 假令十室五逃，則均責未逃者，若抵石於井，非極泉不止，誠繇聚斂之臣割下媚上。

translations.literal: If in ten households five flee, the tax is averaged onto those not fled—like dropping a stone in a well, it does not stop until it reaches the bottom; truly this comes from revenue-grabbing ministers cutting from below to please above.
translations.idiomatic: If five in ten flee, the burden falls on those who remain—like a stone dropped in a well, it sinks until it hits bottom—truly the work of revenue-grabbing ministers who squeeze the people to please their superiors.

sentences.zh: 願下詔一賜禁止，計不三年，人必歸於農。
