translations.literal: I wish an edict would be issued at once forbidding this; within three years people will surely return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict forbidding this at once; within three years the people will return to farming.

sentences.zh: 夫農，國之本，本立而太平可議矣。」

translations.literal: Farming is the foundation of the state; when the foundation is established, great peace may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture is the foundation of the state; when that is firm, peace becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 又言：「道路茀不治，驛馬多死。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Roads are overgrown and untended; relay horses die in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Roads are overgrown and untended; relay horses die in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 憲宗得奏咨駭，即詔出飛龍馬數百給畿驛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong received the memorial with alarm and at once ordered several hundred Flying Dragon horses issued to capital relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was alarmed by the memorial and immediately issued several hundred imperial horses to capital relay stations.

sentences.zh: 渤既以峭直觸要臣意，乃謝病歸。

translations.literal: Bo having offended powerful ministers with his sharp bluntness, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's bluntness offended powerful ministers, and he pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，召拜考功員外郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Merit Examination Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, Bo was summoned as Vice Director of the Merit Examination Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歳終，當校考。

translations.literal: At year's end came the annual performance review.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end came the annual performance review.

sentences.zh: 渤自宰相而下升黜之，上奏曰：「宰相俯、文昌、值，陛下即位，倚以責功，安危治亂系也。

translations.literal: Bo promoted and demoted from chief ministers downward and submitted: "Chief ministers Fu, Wenchang, and Zhi—when Your Majesty acceded you relied on them to assign merit; security, peril, order, and chaos depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo graded officials from chief ministers down and submitted: "Chief ministers Fu, Wenchang, and Zhi—on Your Majesty's accession you relied on them for achievement; the realm's security depends on them.

sentences.zh: 方陛下敬大臣，未有暱比左右自驕之心，而天下事一以付之，俯等不推至公，陳先王道德，又不振拔舊典，復百司之本。

translations.literal: While Your Majesty respects great ministers and has not yet favored close attendants with self-aggrandizing hearts, yet all affairs under Heaven are entrusted to them—Fu and the others do not pursue utmost fairness, set forth the former kings' virtue, nor revive old institutions and restore the foundations of the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty respects great ministers and has not yet favored flatterers, yet entrusts all affairs to them—Fu and his colleagues do not pursue fairness, expound the sages' virtue, or restore old institutions.

sentences.zh: 政之興廢在賞罰。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of governance lies in rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Governance rises or falls on rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 俯等未聞慰一首公，使天下吏有所勸；

translations.literal: Fu and the others have not been heard to comfort a single worthy man, so that officials under Heaven have something to emulate;
translations.idiomatic: They have not rewarded a single worthy official to encourage others;

sentences.zh: 黜一不職，使尸祿有所懼。

translations.literal: nor demoted one incompetent, so that salary-eaters have something to fear.
translations.idiomatic: nor demoted one incompetent to frighten salary-eaters.

sentences.zh: 士之邪正混然無章。

translations.literal: The upright and corrupt among officials are mixed without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy and the corrupt are indistinguishable.

sentences.zh: 陛下比幸驪山，宰相、學士皆股肱心腹，宜皆知之，不先事以諫，陷君於過。

translations.literal: Your Majesty recently visited Mount Li; chief ministers and academicians are your arms, thighs, and heart—they should all have known and remonstrated beforehand, yet they did not, trapping the lord in fault.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty recently visited Mount Li; ministers and academicians are your closest advisers—they should have remonstrated beforehand but did not, leading you into error.

sentences.zh: 俯與學士杜元穎等請考中下。

translations.literal: Fu and Academician Du Yuanying and others should be rated middle-lower.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Academician Du Yuanying should be rated middle-lower.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李絳、左散騎常侍張惟素、右散騎常侍李益諫幸驪山，鄭覃等諫畋游，得事君之禮，請考上下。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiang, Left Regular Attendant Zhang Weisu, and Right Regular Attendant Li Yi remonstrated against visiting Mount Li; Zheng Tan and others remonstrated against hunting—they observed the rites of serving a lord and should be rated upper-middle.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiang, Zhang Weisu, and Li Yi remonstrated against the Mount Li visit; Zheng Tan and others against hunting—they observed proper service and should be rated upper-middle.

sentences.zh: 崔元略當考上下，前考於翬不實，翬以賄死，請降中中。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanlue should be rated upper-middle, but his previous rating of Yu was false—Yu died from bribery—so I ask that he be lowered to middle-middle.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue deserves upper-middle, but his previous rating of Yu was false—Yu died from bribery—so lower him to middle-middle.

sentences.zh: 大理卿許季同，任翬者，應考中下；

translations.literal: Grand Court Judge Xu Jitong, who appointed Yu, should be rated middle-lower;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Court Judge Xu Jitong, who appointed Yu, should be rated middle-lower;

sentences.zh: 然頃陷劉闢，棄家以歸，宜補厥過，考中中。

translations.literal: yet recently when trapped by Liu Pi he abandoned his household to return—this should compensate his fault; rate middle-middle.
translations.idiomatic: yet when trapped by Liu Pi he abandoned his household to return—this compensates his fault; rate middle-middle.

sentences.zh: 少府監裴通職修舉，考應中上；

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Storehouse Pei Tong performed his duties well and should be rated middle-upper;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Storehouse Pei Tong performed well and deserves middle-upper;

sentences.zh: 以封母，舍嫡而追所生，請考中下。」

translations.literal: for ennobling his mother he abandoned the principal wife to honor his birth mother—rate middle-lower.
translations.idiomatic: for ennobling his birth mother he abandoned his principal wife—rate middle-lower.

sentences.zh: 奏入，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 會渤請急，馮宿領考功，以「考課令取歳中善惡爲上下，郎中校京官四品以下黜陟之，由三品上爲清望官，歳進名聽內考，非有司所得專。

translations.literal: When Bo requested urgent leave, Feng Su headed the Merit Examination Bureau and argued: "The examination regulations take good and bad within the year as upper and lower; directors review capital officials of fourth rank and below for promotion and demotion; from third rank upward are prestigious offices whose annual names are submitted for internal review—not something the relevant offices may decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo took urgent leave, Feng Su headed the Merit Examination Bureau and argued: "Regulations require grading officials by their year's performance; directors review officials below fourth rank; third rank and above are prestigious posts reviewed internally—not something outside offices may decide alone.

sentences.zh: 渤舉舊事爲褒貶，違朝廷制，請如故事」。

translations.literal: Bo cited old precedents for praise and blame, violating court regulations—please follow established practice."
translations.idiomatic: Bo cited old precedents in violation of regulations—follow established practice."

sentences.zh: 渤議遂廢。

translations.literal: Bo's proposal was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 會魏博節度使田弘正表渤爲副，元穎劾奏：「渤賣直售名，資狂躁，干進不已，外交方鎮求尉薦，不宜在朝。」

translations.literal: When Weibo Military Commissioner Tian Hongzheng recommended Bo as deputy, Yuanying impeached: "Bo sells bluntness to buy fame, relies on rash impetuosity, ceaselessly seeks advancement, and cultivates frontier commanders for recommendations—he should not remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Weibo Commissioner Tian Hongzheng recommended Bo as deputy, Yuanying impeached him: "Bo sells bluntness for fame, is rash and restless, ceaselessly seeks advancement, and cultivates frontier commanders for patronage—he should not remain at court.

sentences.zh: 出爲虔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Qian.

sentences.zh: 渤奏還信州移稅錢二百萬，免賦米二萬石，廢冗役千六百人。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized returning two million in transferred tax money to Xin prefecture, exempting twenty thousand piculs of grain tax, and abolishing sixteen hundred superfluous corvée workers.
translations.idiomatic: Bo returned two million in transferred tax money to Xin prefecture, exempted twenty thousand piculs of grain tax, and abolished sixteen hundred superfluous corvée workers.

sentences.zh: 觀察使上狀。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner submitted a report upward.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner reported his achievements to the throne.

sentences.zh: 不閱歳，遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: Within less than a year he was transferred to prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was transferred to prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 度支使張平叔斂天下逋租，渤上言：「度支所收貞元二年流戸賦錢四百四十萬，臣州治田二千頃，今旱死者千九百頃。

translations.literal: Revenue Commissioner Zhang Pingshu collected delinquent rents throughout the realm; Bo submitted: "The Revenue Bureau collects four million four hundred thousand in fugitive-household taxes from the second year of Zhenyuan; in my prefecture there are two thousand qing of administered fields, of which one thousand nine hundred qing have died from drought.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Commissioner Zhang Pingshu collected delinquent rents empire-wide. Bo wrote: "The Revenue Bureau collects 4.4 million in fugitive-household taxes from Zhenyuan 2; my prefecture has two thousand qing of fields, of which nineteen hundred qing have died from drought.

sentences.zh: 若徇度支所斂，臣懼天下謂陛下當大旱責民三十年逋賦。

translations.literal: If I follow what the Revenue Bureau collects, I fear the realm will say Your Majesty, amid great drought, is extracting thirty years of delinquent taxes from the people.
translations.idiomatic: If I enforce this collection, I fear the realm will say Your Majesty is extracting thirty years of back taxes during a great drought.

sentences.zh: 臣刺史，上不能奉詔，下不忍民窮，無所逃死，請放歸田里。」

translations.literal: I am a prefect—above I cannot obey the edict, below I cannot bear the people's destitution; with nowhere to flee but death, I ask to be released to return to my fields.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect I cannot obey the edict above yet cannot bear the people's destitution below; with nowhere to turn, I ask to be released to my fields.

sentences.zh: 有詔蠲責。

translations.literal: An edict remitted the collection.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted the collection.

sentences.zh: 渤又治湖水，築堤七百步，使人不病涉。

translations.literal: Bo also managed the lake waters and built a dike seven hundred paces long, so people were not troubled crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also managed the lake, built a seven-hundred-pace dike, and spared people the hardship of crossing.

sentences.zh: 入爲職方郎中，進諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Bureau of Appointments and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Director of the Bureau of Appointments and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 時敬宗晏朝紫宸，入閣，帝久不出，群臣立屏外，至頓僕。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Jingzong delayed court at Purple Audience Hall; entering the side hall, the emperor long did not appear; officials stood outside the screen until they collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong delayed court at Purple Audience Hall; entering the side hall, the emperor long failed to appear, and officials standing outside the screen collapsed from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 渤見宰相曰：「昨論晏朝事，今益晚，是諫官不能移人主意，渤請出閣待罪。」

translations.literal: Bo saw the chief ministers and said: "Yesterday we discussed delayed court; today it is even later—this shows remonstrance officials cannot move men's minds; Bo asks to leave the hall and await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bo told the chief ministers: "Yesterday we discussed delayed court; today it is even later—remonstrance officials cannot move the emperor's mind; I ask to leave the hall and await punishment.

sentences.zh: 會喚仗，乃止。

translations.literal: Just then the guard was summoned and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the guard was summoned and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 退上疏曰：「今日入閣，陛下不時見群臣，群臣皆布路跛倚。

translations.literal: Retiring he submitted a memorial: "Today entering the side hall, Your Majesty did not promptly receive officials; all officials stood scattered along the road, limping and leaning.
translations.idiomatic: He later memorialized: "Today entering the side hall, Your Majesty did not promptly receive officials; all stood scattered along the road, limping and leaning.

sentences.zh: 夫跛倚形諸外，則憂思結諸內。

translations.literal: When limping and leaning appear outwardly, worry and thought bind inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: When exhaustion shows outwardly, worry binds inwardly.

sentences.zh: 憂倦既積，災釁必生，小則爲旱爲孽，大則爲兵爲亂。

translations.literal: When worry and weariness accumulate, calamity and misfortune must arise—small ones drought and pestilence, great ones war and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When worry and weariness accumulate, calamity follows—small ones drought and pestilence, great ones war and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：『三諫不聽，則逃之。』

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: 'If thrice remonstrated and not heeded, then flee.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: 'If thrice remonstrated and not heeded, then flee.'

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，臣至三諫，恐危及社稷。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly acceded; I have remonstrated thrice—I fear the altars of state will be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly acceded; I have remonstrated thrice—I fear for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 又言：「左右常侍職規諷，循默不事，若設官不責實，不如罷之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Left and Right Regular Attendants have the duty of remonstrance yet follow in silence and do nothing—if offices are established without demanding performance, better abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Left and Right Regular Attendants have the duty of remonstrance yet remain silent—if offices are established without demanding performance, better abolish them.

sentences.zh: 俄充理匭使，建言：「事大者以聞，次白宰相，下以移有司。

translations.literal: Soon he served as commissioner for the complaint box and proposed: "Great matters should be reported upward; next inform the chief ministers; lesser ones transfer to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as commissioner for the complaint box and proposed: "Great matters should reach the throne; next inform chief ministers; lesser ones go to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 有司不當，許再納匭。

translations.literal: If the relevant offices handle wrongly, allow resubmission to the box.
translations.idiomatic: If offices handle a case wrongly, allow resubmission to the box.

sentences.zh: 妄訴者加所坐一等，以絶冒越。」

translations.literal: For false complaints increase the penalty one degree to cut off presumptuous overreach.
translations.idiomatic: For false complaints increase the penalty one degree to deter abuse.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 時政移近幸，紀律蕩然，渤勁正不顧患，通章封無闋日。

translations.literal: At the time government shifted to close favorites and discipline collapsed utterly; Bo was forceful and upright without regard for peril, submitting sealed memorials without a day's interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Government had shifted to favorites and discipline collapsed; Bo remonstrated bluntly without fear, submitting memorials day after day.

sentences.zh: 天子雖幼昏，亦感寤，擢給事中，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: Though the Son of Heaven was young and dull, he was also moved to awareness, promoted Bo to Supervising Censor, and bestowed gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Though young and unsteady, the emperor was moved and promoted Bo to Supervising Censor, granting gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 五坊卒夜鬪，傷縣人，鄠令崔發怒，敕吏捕捽，其一，中人也，釋之。

translations.literal: Soldiers of the Five Wards fought at night and injured a county man; Magistrate Cui Fa of E grew angry and ordered officials to seize them; one was a eunuch and was released.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of the Five Wards fought at night and injured a county man; Magistrate Cui Fa of E ordered their arrest, but one was a eunuch and was released.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，收發送御史獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, arrested Fa, and sent him to the censor's prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, arrested Fa, and sent him to the censor's prison.

sentences.zh: 會大赦、改元，發以囚坐雞竽下，俄而中人數十持梃亂擊，發敗面折齒，幾死，吏哀請乃去。

translations.literal: When a general amnesty and era change occurred, Fa as prisoner sat below the cock-and-reed instrument; soon several dozen eunuchs with clubs beat him randomly; Fa's face was ruined and teeth broken, nearly dying; officials pleaded in grief before they left.
translations.idiomatic: During a general amnesty and era change, Fa sat shackled below the court musicians; soon dozens of eunuchs beat him with clubs, breaking his face and teeth; he nearly died before officials pleaded them away.

sentences.zh: 既而囚皆釋，而發不得原。

translations.literal: Soon all prisoners were released, but Fa was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all prisoners were released, but Fa was not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 渤上疏曰：「縣令曳辱中人，中人毆御囚，其罪一也。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial: "The magistrate dragged and shamed a eunuch; the eunuch beat an imperial prisoner—their crimes are one.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized: "The magistrate dragged and shamed a eunuch; the eunuch beat an imperial prisoner—their crimes are equal.

sentences.zh: 然令罪在赦前，而中人在赦後，不寘於法，臣恐四夷聞之，慢倍之心生矣。」

translations.literal: Yet the magistrate's crime was before the amnesty while the eunuch's was after; not placing them under the law—I fear when the four barbarians hear this, hearts of contempt and defiance will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the magistrate's crime preceded the amnesty while the eunuch's came after; if the law is not applied equally, I fear barbarians will learn contempt.

sentences.zh: 渤又誦言：「前神策軍在幔城，篡京兆進食牙盤，不時治，致宦人益橫。」

translations.literal: Bo also cited: "Formerly when the Divine Strategy Army was in the curtained city, they usurped the Capital Prefect's food-serving trays and were not promptly punished, causing eunuchs to grow more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also cited: "When the Divine Strategy Army was in the curtained city, they seized the Capital Prefect's food service and went unpunished, making eunuchs ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 帝以問左右，皆曰「無之」。

translations.literal: The emperor asked his attendants; all said "Nothing of the sort."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his attendants; all denied it.

sentences.zh: 帝謂渤有黨，出爲桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor said Bo had a faction and sent him out as Guiguan Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Bo had a faction and sent him out as Guiguan Observation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 它日，宰相李逢吉等見帝曰：「發暴中人，誠不敬，然其母故宰相韋貫之姊，年八十，憂發成疾。

translations.literal: Another day Chief Minister Li Fengji and others saw the emperor and said: "Fa assaulted a eunuch—truly disrespectful; yet his mother is the elder sister of former chief minister Wei Guanzhi, eighty years old, sick with worry over Fa.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Chief Minister Li Fengji told the emperor: "Fa assaulted a eunuch—truly disrespectful; yet his mother, elder sister of former chief minister Wei Guanzhi, is eighty and sick with worry.

sentences.zh: 陛下方孝治，宜少延之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just establishing filial governance and should extend him a little mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is establishing filial governance and should show mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝惻然曰：「比諫官但言發枉，未嘗道此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with compassion: "Recently remonstrance officials only spoke of Fa's injustice and never mentioned this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said compassionately: "Remonstrance officials spoke only of Fa's injustice and never mentioned this.

sentences.zh: 即遣使送發於家，且撫尉其母。

translations.literal: He at once sent an envoy to return Fa to his home and comfort his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent Fa home and comforted his mother.

sentences.zh: 韋拜詔，泣對使者杖發四十。

translations.literal: Wei received the edict, wept before the envoy, and had Fa beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received the edict, wept before the envoy, and had Fa beaten forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 猶奪其官。

translations.literal: His office was still taken away.
translations.idiomatic: His office was still taken away.

sentences.zh: 至文宗，乃用發爲懷州長史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wenzong, Fa was finally employed as chief administrator of Huai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wenzong, Fa was finally appointed chief administrator of Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 桂有漓水，出海陽山，世言秦命史祿伐粵，鑿爲漕，馬援討徵側，復治以通饋；

translations.literal: Gui had the Li River, issuing from Haiyang Mountain; tradition says Qin ordered Shi Lu to attack Yue and cut it as a canal; Ma Yuan campaigning against Zheng Ce restored it for transport;
translations.idiomatic: Gui had the Li River, flowing from Haiyang Mountain; tradition says Qin ordered Shi Lu to cut a canal when attacking Yue; Ma Yuan restored it when campaigning against Zheng Ce;

sentences.zh: 後爲江水潰毀，渠遂廢淺，每轉餉，役數十戸濟一艘。

translations.literal: later the Yangzi waters burst and destroyed it, the channel was abandoned and shallow, and for each transport of supplies dozens of households were conscripted to move one boat.
translations.idiomatic: later Yangzi floods destroyed it; the channel silted up, and dozens of households were conscripted to move each supply boat.

sentences.zh: 渤釃浚舊道，鄣洩有宜，舟楫利焉。

translations.literal: Bo performed libation and dredged the old route, blocking leaks appropriately, and boats benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Bo dredged the old channel, repaired the dikes, and restored boat traffic.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以病歸洛。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned to Luoyang due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he returned to Luoyang due to illness.

sentences.zh: 大和中，召拜太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era he was summoned and appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era he was summoned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-nine and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 渤，孤操自將，不茍合於世，人咸謂之沽激。

translations.literal: Bo maintained solitary integrity and would not compromise with the world; all called him ostentatious and provocative.
translations.idiomatic: Bo held himself aloof and would not compromise; many called him ostentatious.

sentences.zh: 屢以言斥，而悻直不少衰，守節者尚之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly expelled for his words, his stubborn bluntness did not diminish; men who kept integrity admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly expelled for his words, his blunt integrity never faded; men of principle admired him.

sentences.zh: 裴潾，本河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Lin was originally from Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Lin was from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 篤學，善隸書。

translations.literal: He studied deeply and was skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He was a devoted scholar and skilled in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 以廕仕。

translations.literal: He entered office by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 元和初，累遷左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was repeatedly promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he rose to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 於是兩河用兵，憲宗任宦人爲館驛使，檢稽出納。

translations.literal: At this time the Two He regions were at war; Emperor Xianzong appointed eunuchs as relay station commissioners to inspect receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: During the Two He campaign, Xianzong appointed eunuchs as relay station commissioners to inspect finances.

sentences.zh: 有曹進玉者，尤恃恩倨甚，使者過，至加捽辱，宰相李吉甫奏罷之。

translations.literal: One Cao Jinyu was especially arrogant relying on favor; when envoys passed he even added beating and insult; Chief Minister Li Jifu memorialized to abolish the post.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jinyu was especially arrogant; he even beat and insulted passing envoys; Chief Minister Li Jifu had the post abolished.

sentences.zh: 會伐蔡，復以中人領使。

translations.literal: When Cai was attacked, eunuchs again headed the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was attacked, eunuchs again headed the commission.

sentences.zh: 潾諫曰：「凡驛，有官專尸之，畿內以京兆尹，道有觀察使、刺史相監臨，臺又御史爲之使，以察過闕。

translations.literal: Lin remonstrated: "Relay stations in general have dedicated officials; within the capital the Capital Prefect, on the circuits observation commissioners and prefects mutually supervise, and the Censorate also sends censors as envoys to inspect faults and lapses.
translations.idiomatic: Lin remonstrated: "Relay stations have dedicated officials—the Capital Prefect within the capital, observation commissioners and prefects on the circuits, and censors from the Censorate to inspect faults.

sentences.zh: 猶有不職，則宜明科條督責之，誰不惕懼？

translations.literal: If there is still dereliction, regulations should be clarified to supervise and hold accountable—who would not be wary and fearful?
translations.idiomatic: If dereliction remains, clarify regulations and hold officials accountable—who would not fear?

sentences.zh: 若復以宮闈臣領之，則內人而及外事，職分亂矣。

translations.literal: If palace inner attendants again head it, then inner persons reach outer affairs and duties are confused.
translations.idiomatic: If palace eunuchs head it again, inner attendants will reach into outer affairs and duties will be confused.

sentences.zh: 夫事不善，誡於初；

translations.literal: When affairs are not good, warn at the beginning;
translations.idiomatic: When affairs go wrong, warn at the start;

sentences.zh: 體有非，不必大。

translations.literal: when the system has fault, it need not be great.
translations.idiomatic: when the system errs, the error need not be great.

sentences.zh: 方開太平，澄本正末，宜塞侵官之原、出位之漸。」

translations.literal: Just as great peace is opening, clarify the root and correct the branch; one should block the source of encroaching offices and the first steps of overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: As great peace opens, clarify roots and correct branches; block encroaching offices and overstepping duties.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不用，而嘉其忠，擢起居舍人。

translations.literal: The emperor though he did not adopt this praised his loyalty and promoted him to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt this but praised his loyalty and promoted him to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 帝喜方士，而柳泌爲帝治丹劑，求長年。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in alchemists; Liu Bi prepared elixir pills for the emperor seeking long life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in alchemists; Liu Bi prepared elixirs seeking long life.

sentences.zh: 帝御劑，中躁病渴。

translations.literal: The emperor took the elixir and suffered agitation, illness, and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the elixir and suffered agitation, illness, and thirst.

sentences.zh: 潾諫曰：

translations.literal: Lin remonstrated:
translations.idiomatic: Lin remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 夫除天下之害者，常受天下之利；

translations.literal: Those who remove harm under Heaven constantly receive benefit under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Those who remove the realm's harm receive the realm's benefit;

sentences.zh: 共天下之樂者，常饗天下之福。

translations.literal: those who share joy under Heaven constantly enjoy fortune under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: those who share the realm's joy enjoy the realm's fortune.

sentences.zh: 故上自黃帝、顓頊、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，咸以功濟生人，天皆報以耆壽，垂榮無疆。

translations.literal: Thus from the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu upward—all with achievement aiding the living, Heaven repaid each with long life and boundless enduring glory.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—all aided the people by merit, and Heaven rewarded them with long life and lasting glory.

sentences.zh: 陛下以孝安宗廟，以仁牧黎庶，攘剗襖兇，復張太平，賓禮賢俊，待以終始。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with filial piety settles the ancestral temples, with benevolence governs the common people, sweeps away evil rebels, restores great peace, treats worthy men as guests with courtesy from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty settles the ancestral temples with filial piety, governs the people with benevolence, sweeps away rebels, restores peace, and honors worthy men from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 神功聖德，前古所不及。

translations.literal: Divine achievement and sage virtue—antiquity cannot match them.
translations.idiomatic: Divine achievement and sage virtue surpass antiquity.

sentences.zh: 陛下躬行之，天地宗廟必相陛下以億萬之永。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally practices this; Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples will surely assist Your Majesty to endless myriads of years.
translations.idiomatic: Practice this personally and Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples will grant endless years.

sentences.zh: 今乃方士韋山甫、柳泌等以丹術自神，更相稱引，詭爲陛下延年。

translations.literal: Now alchemists Wei Shanfu, Liu Bi, and others make themselves divine through elixir arts, mutually recommending one another, falsely claiming to extend Your Majesty's years.
translations.idiomatic: Now alchemists Wei Shanfu, Liu Bi, and others pose as divine through elixirs, recommending one another and falsely promising long life.

sentences.zh: 臣謂士有道者皆匿名滅景，無求於世，豈肯干謁貴近，自鬻其伎哉？

translations.literal: I say men of the Way all hide their names and extinguish their traces, seeking nothing from the world—would they willingly importune the noble and near and sell their arts?
translations.idiomatic: Men of the Way hide their names and seek nothing from the world—would they importune the powerful and sell their arts?

sentences.zh: 今所至者，非曰知道，咸求利而來。

translations.literal: Those who arrive now do not truly know the Way; all come seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who come now do not know the Way; all come seeking profit.

sentences.zh: 自言飛煉爲神，以訹權賄，僞窮情得，不恥遁亡。

translations.literal: They claim transmutation and refinement make them divine, use threats and bribes, feign exhaustive understanding, and are not ashamed to flee when exposed.
translations.idiomatic: They claim transmutation makes them divine, use threats and bribes, feign wisdom, and flee without shame when exposed.

sentences.zh: 豈可信厥術、御其藥哉？

translations.literal: How can one trust their arts or take their medicines?
translations.idiomatic: How can one trust their arts or take their medicines?

sentences.zh: 臣聞人食味、別聲、被色而生者也。

translations.literal: I have heard that humans live by tasting flavors, distinguishing sounds, and receiving colors.
translations.idiomatic: Humans live by tasting flavors, distinguishing sounds, and receiving colors.

sentences.zh: 味以行氣，氣以實志。

translations.literal: Flavor moves qi; qi fills the will.
translations.idiomatic: Flavor moves qi; qi fills the will.

sentences.zh: 水火鹽梅以烹魚肉，宰夫和之，齊之以味，君子食之，以平其心。

translations.literal: Water, fire, salt, and plum sauce cook fish and meat; the cook harmonizes them and balances flavors; the gentleman eats to settle his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Water, fire, salt, and plum sauce cook fish and meat; the cook balances flavors; the gentleman eats to settle his heart.

sentences.zh: 夫三牲五穀，稟五行以生也，發爲五味。

translations.literal: The three sacrificial animals and five grains receive the five phases to be born and manifest as the five flavors.
translations.idiomatic: The three sacrificial animals and five grains are born of the five phases and manifest as the five flavors.

sentences.zh: 天地生之，所以奉人，聖人節調，以致康強。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth produce them to serve humans; sages regulate them to achieve health and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth produce them to serve humans; sages regulate them for health and strength.

sentences.zh: 若乃藥劑者，所以御疾，豈常進之餌哉？

translations.literal: As for medicines, they are to control illness—how can they be regular daily food?
translations.idiomatic: Medicines control illness—how can they be daily food?

sentences.zh: 況又金石性托酷烈，而燒治積年，包炎產毒，未易可制。

translations.literal: Moreover minerals and metals are by nature fiercely harsh; refined over accumulated years they wrap heat and produce poison—not easily controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Minerals and metals are fiercely harsh; refined over years they produce poison not easily controlled.

sentences.zh: 夫秦、漢之君亦信方士矣，如盧生、徐福、欒大、李少君，後皆詐譎無成功。

translations.literal: Emperors of Qin and Han also trusted alchemists—Lu Sheng, Xu Fu, Luan Da, Li Shaojun—all later proved deceitful without success.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han emperors also trusted alchemists—Lu Sheng, Xu Fu, Luan Da, Li Shaojun—all proved deceitful failures.

sentences.zh: 事暴前策，皆可驗視。

translations.literal: These matters are exposed in former records and can all be verified.
translations.idiomatic: These matters are recorded in history and can all be verified.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：「君之藥，臣先嘗之；

translations.literal: The Book of Rites: "The lord's medicine—the minister tastes it first;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites: "The lord's medicine—the minister tastes it first;

sentences.zh: 父之藥，子先嘗之。」

translations.literal: the father's medicine—the son tastes it first.
translations.idiomatic: the father's medicine—the son tastes it first.

sentences.zh: 臣、子一也，願以所治劑，俾其人服之，竟一歳以考真僞，則無不驗矣。

translations.literal: Minister and son are one; I wish the elixir they prepare be given them to take for a full year to test truth and falsehood—then nothing will fail verification.
translations.idiomatic: Minister and son are alike; let them take their own elixir for a full year to test its truth—then nothing will fail verification.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶江陵令。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and demoted him to magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and demoted him to magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，泌等誅，召潾，再遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, Bi and others were executed; Lin was summoned and twice promoted to Director of the Penalties Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, Bi and others were executed; Lin was summoned and promoted to Director of the Penalties Bureau.

sentences.zh: 前率府倉曹參軍曲元衡杖民柏公成母死，有司以死在辜外，推元衡父廕贖金，公成受賕不訴，以赦免。

translations.literal: Formerly Lead Palace Granary Assistant Qu Yuanheng beat commoner Bai Gongcheng's mother to death; officials held the death outside the mourning period and applied Yuanheng's father's yin privilege for redemption; Gongcheng took bribes and did not prosecute and was pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Lead Palace Granary Assistant Qu Yuanheng beat commoner Bai Gongcheng's mother to death; officials applied Yuanheng's father's yin privilege for redemption; Gongcheng took bribes and did not prosecute and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 潾議曰：「杖捶者，官得施所部，非所部，雖有罪，必請有司，明不可擅也。

translations.literal: Lin argued: "Beating may be applied by officials only within their jurisdiction; outside their jurisdiction, even if guilty, they must request the relevant offices—clearly they may not act on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued: "Officials may beat only within their jurisdiction; outside it they must refer to the relevant offices—they may not act on their own.

sentences.zh: 元衡非在官，公成母非所部，不可以廕免。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was not in office; Gongcheng's mother was not within his jurisdiction—yin privilege cannot exempt him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng was not in office and Gongcheng's mother was not within his jurisdiction—yin privilege cannot exempt him.

sentences.zh: 公成取賄仇家，利母之死，逆天性，當伏誅。」

translations.literal: Gongcheng took bribes from the enemy household and profited from his mother's death—against human nature; he should suffer execution.
translations.idiomatic: Gongcheng took bribes from his enemy and profited from his mother's death—against nature; he should be executed.

sentences.zh: 有詔元衡流，公成論死。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuanheng exiled and Gongcheng sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exiled Yuanheng and sentenced Gongcheng to death.

sentences.zh: 久之，繇給事中爲汝州刺史，越法杖人輒死，以太子左庶子分司東都。

translations.literal: After a long time, from Supervising Censor he became prefect of Ru; exceeding the law he beat people to death and was made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent serving in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Supervising Censor he became prefect of Ru; exceeding the law he beat a man to death and was made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 遷左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎，爲華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Penalties and made prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Penalties and prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部侍郎，出爲河南尹，復還舊官。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of War, sent out as Henan Intendant, and returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of War, served as Henan Intendant, and returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈戸部尚書，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue with posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 潾以道自任，悉心事上，疾黨附，不爲權近所持。

translations.literal: Lin took the Way as his charge, devoted himself wholly to serving the sovereign, hated factional attachment, and was not controlled by powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Lin took the Way as his charge, served the sovereign wholeheartedly, hated faction, and was not controlled by powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 嘗裒古今辭章，續梁昭明太子《文選》，自號《大和通選》，上之。

translations.literal: He once collected ancient and modern literary compositions, continuing Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang's Literary Selections, calling it Comprehensive Selections of Dahe, and submitted it upward.
translations.idiomatic: He collected ancient and modern literary compositions, continuing Crown Prince Zhaoming's Literary Selections in his Comprehensive Selections of Dahe, and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 當時文士非與游者皆不取，世恨其隘。

translations.literal: Literati of the time not associated with him were all excluded; the world resented his narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: He excluded all literati not in his circle; the world resented his narrowness.

sentences.zh: 憲宗竟以藥棄天下，世益謂潾知言。

translations.literal: Xianzong ultimately abandoned the realm through medicine; the world increasingly said Lin had known how to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ultimately died from elixirs; the world increasingly said Lin had spoken truly.

sentences.zh: 穆宗雖誅泌，而後稍稍復惑方士。

translations.literal: Though Muzong executed Bi, afterward he gradually again became deluded by alchemists.
translations.idiomatic: Though Muzong executed Bi, he gradually again fell under alchemists' sway.

sentences.zh: 有布衣張皋者，上疏曰：「神慮澹則血氣和，嗜欲勝則疾疹作。

translations.literal: There was a commoner Zhang Gao who submitted a memorial: "When the spirit's thoughts are calm, blood and qi are harmonious; when desires prevail, illness arises.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner Zhang Gao memorialized: "When the spirit is calm, blood and qi are harmonious; when desires prevail, illness arises.

sentences.zh: 古之聖賢務自頤養，不以外物橈耳目、聲色敗情性，繇是和平自臻，福慶用昌。

translations.literal: Ancient sages strove to nourish themselves, not letting outer things disturb eyes and ears or sound and color ruin nature—thereby harmony came of itself and fortune flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sages nourished themselves, not letting outer things disturb the senses or ruin nature—thereby harmony came and fortune flourished.

sentences.zh: 在《易》，『無妄之疾，勿藥有喜』，在《詩》『自天降康，降福穰穰』，此天人符也。

translations.literal: In the Book of Changes: 'Illness without cause—do not medicate and there will be joy'; in the Book of Songs: 'From Heaven comes peace, blessings abundant'—this is Heaven and human in accord.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'Illness without cause—do not medicate and there will be joy'; the Book of Songs says: 'From Heaven comes peace, blessings abundant'—Heaven and human are in accord.

sentences.zh: 然則藥以攻疾，無疾不用藥也。

translations.literal: Thus medicine attacks illness; without illness do not use medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine attacks illness; without illness do not use medicine.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，處士孫思邈達於養生，其言曰：『人無故不應餌藥。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time the recluse Sun Simiao was accomplished in nourishing life; he said: 'People without cause should not take medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's time recluse Sun Simiao mastered nourishing life; he said: 'People without cause should not take medicine.

sentences.zh: 藥有所偏助，則藏氣爲不平。』

translations.literal: When medicine partially assists, the visceral qi becomes unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: When medicine partially assists, visceral qi becomes unbalanced.

sentences.zh: 推此論之，可謂達見至理。

translations.literal: Extending this argument, it may be called penetrating insight into supreme principle.
translations.idiomatic: This is penetrating insight into supreme principle.

sentences.zh: 夫寒暑爲賊，節宣乖度，有資於醫，尚當重慎。

translations.literal: Cold and heat are assailants; when regulation and dispersal miss measure, medicine may help—yet one should still be deeply cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat are assailants; when the body's rhythms fail, medicine may help—yet caution is still required.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》稱：『醫不三世，不服其藥。』

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Rites says: 'If the physician is not of three generations, do not take his medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: 'If the physician is not of three generations, do not take his medicine.

sentences.zh: 庶士猶爾，況天子乎？

translations.literal: Common scholars are still thus—how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Common scholars are still thus—how much more the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 先帝晚節喜方士，累致危疾，陛下所自知，不可蹈前覆、迎後梅也。

translations.literal: The former emperor in his late years delighted in alchemists and repeatedly brought on dangerous illness—Your Majesty knows this yourself; one must not tread the former overturning and invite later regret.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor in his late years delighted in alchemists and repeatedly fell dangerously ill—as Your Majesty knows; do not repeat past disaster and invite future regret.

sentences.zh: 今人人竊議，直畏忤旨，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Now everyone privately discusses this but fears only offending the imperial will and dares not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Now everyone privately discusses this but fears offending the throne and dares not speak.

sentences.zh: 臣蓬菣之生，非以邀寵，顧忠義可爲者，聞而默，則不安，願陛下無忽。」

translations.literal: I am a humble weed—not to seek favor; yet where loyalty and righteousness can act, to hear and remain silent brings unease; I wish Your Majesty not to neglect this.
translations.idiomatic: I am a humble weed—not seeking favor; yet where loyalty demands speech, silence brings unease; I beg Your Majesty not to neglect this.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，詔訪皋，不獲。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words and ordered Gao sought, but he was not found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words and ordered Gao sought, but he was not found.

sentences.zh: 李中敏，字藏之，系出隴西。

translations.literal: Li Zhongmin, courtesy name Cangzhi, was descended from Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongmin, styled Cangzhi, was descended from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 元和中，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性剛峭，與杜牧、李甘善，其文辭氣節大抵相上下。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and sharp; he was friendly with Du Mu and Li Gan; their literary style and moral integrity were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and uncompromising, friendly with Du Mu and Li Gan; their literary talent and integrity were roughly equal.

sentences.zh: 沈傳師觀察江西，闢爲判官。

translations.literal: When Shen Chuanshi was observation commissioner of Jiangxi, he recruited Zhongmin as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Chuanshi was Jiangxi observation commissioner, he recruited Zhongmin as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 入拜侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and was appointed Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 鄭注誣逐宰相宋申錫，天下以目。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu falsely drove out Chief Minister Song Shenxi; all under Heaven watched with eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu falsely drove out Chief Minister Song Shenxi; the whole realm watched in silence.

sentences.zh: 大和六年，大旱，文宗內憂，詔詢所以致雨者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe, great drought came; Emperor Wenzong was inwardly troubled and issued an edict inquiring how to bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 6, a great drought struck; Wenzong was deeply troubled and issued an edict asking how to bring rain.

sentences.zh: 中敏時以司門員外郎上言：「雨不時降，夏陽驕愆，苗欲槁枯，陛下憂勤，降德音，俾下得盡言。

translations.literal: Zhongmin at the time as Vice Director of the Gate Bureau submitted: "Rain does not fall in season; summer sun is arrogant and excessive; seedlings are about to wither; Your Majesty is troubled and diligent, issuing gracious words, enabling subjects below to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin, then Vice Director of the Gate Bureau, submitted: "Rain fails to fall; the summer sun is excessive; crops wither; Your Majesty is troubled and has issued gracious words enabling full remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昔東海誤殺一孝婦，大旱三年。

translations.literal: I have heard that formerly in Donghai a filial woman was wrongly killed and drought lasted three years.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in Donghai a filial woman was wrongly killed and drought lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 臣頃爲御史臺推囚，華封儒殺良家子三人，陛下赦封儒死。

translations.literal: I recently as censorate investigator handled prisoners; Hua Fengru killed three sons of good families; Your Majesty pardoned Fengru from death.
translations.idiomatic: I recently investigated prisoners for the censorate; Hua Fengru killed three sons of good families; Your Majesty pardoned him from death.

sentences.zh: 然三人者，亦陛下赤子也。

translations.literal: Yet those three were also Your Majesty's own children.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those three were also Your Majesty's own children.

sentences.zh: 神策士李秀殺平民，法當死，以禁衛，刑止流。

translations.literal: Divine Strategy soldier Li Xiu killed a commoner—by law he should die; because he was imperial guard, punishment stopped at exile.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Strategy soldier Li Xiu killed a commoner—by law he should die; as imperial guard his punishment was reduced to exile.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫位宰相，生平饋致一不受，其道勁正，奸人忌之，陷不測之辜，獄不參驗，銜恨而沒，天下士皆指目鄭注。

translations.literal: Song Shenxi held the chief ministership; in life he accepted not one gift; his Way was forceful and upright; villains envied him; he was trapped in unforeseen guilt; the case was not fully verified; he died bearing resentment; gentlemen under Heaven all pointed at Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi as chief minister accepted no gift in life; his integrity was fierce; villains envied him; he was trapped on unverified charges and died in resentment; gentlemen throughout the realm all pointed at Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 臣知數冤必列訴上帝，天之降災，殆有由然。

translations.literal: I know that accumulated wrongs must be laid before Heaven in appeal; Heaven's sending calamity probably has its cause.
translations.idiomatic: I know accumulated wrongs must be laid before Heaven; Heaven's calamity surely has its cause.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝國用空竭，桑弘羊興筦榷之利，然卜式請亨以致雨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's state revenues were exhausted; Sang Hongyang established monopoly profits; yet Bu Shi requested sacrifice to bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's treasury was exhausted and Sang Hongyang established monopolies; yet Bu Shi offered sacrifice to bring rain.

sentences.zh: 況申錫之枉，天下知之，何惜斬一注以快忠臣之魂，則天且雨矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Shenxi's injustice—the realm knows it—why hesitate to execute Zhu to satisfy the loyal minister's spirit? Then Heaven will rain.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi's injustice is known to all—why hesitate to execute Zhu to satisfy a loyal minister's spirit? Then Heaven will rain.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 中敏以病告滿，歸潁陽。

translations.literal: Zhongmin's sick leave expired and he returned to Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin's sick leave expired and he returned to Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 注誅，以司勛員外郎召。

translations.literal: When Zhu was executed he was summoned as Vice Director of the Merit Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu's execution he was summoned as Vice Director of the Merit Bureau.

sentences.zh: 累遷諫議大夫，爲理匭使，建言：「上書者將納於匭，有司先審其副，有不可，輒卻之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Grandee and served as commissioner for the complaint box, proposing: "When memorial writers are about to submit to the box, relevant offices first review the copy; if unacceptable, they reject it.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Remonstrance Grandee and served as complaint box commissioner, proposing: "When memorials are submitted to the box, officials first review copies and reject unacceptable ones.

sentences.zh: 臣謂匭出禁中，暮而入，爲下開必達之路，廣聰明，直枉結。

translations.literal: I say the box leaves the inner palace and enters at dusk, opening a path of certain access for those below, broadening intelligence and straightening wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: The box leaves the inner palace and returns at dusk, opening certain access for subjects, broadening intelligence and righting wrongs.

sentences.zh: 若有司先裁可否，恐事不重密，非窮塞得自申意。

translations.literal: If relevant offices first judge acceptability, I fear matters will not be kept confidential and the utterly blocked cannot express their intent.
translations.idiomatic: If officials judge acceptability first, matters will not stay confidential and the desperate cannot speak freely.

sentences.zh: 請一裁諸上。」

translations.literal: I ask that judgment rest solely with the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Let judgment rest solely with the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 仇士良以開府階廕其子，中敏曰：「內謁者監安得有子？」

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang used his grand opening rank to grant yin privilege to his son; Zhongmin said: "How can the Director of Inner Attendants have a son?
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang used his grand opening rank to grant yin privilege to his son; Zhongmin said: "How can the Director of Inner Attendants have a son?

sentences.zh: 士良慚恚。

translations.literal: Shiliang was ashamed and enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was ashamed and enraged.

sentences.zh: 繇是復棄官去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he again abandoned office and left.

sentences.zh: 開成末，爲婺、杭二州刺史，卒於官。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaicheng he was prefect of Wu and Hang prefectures and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaicheng he was prefect of Wu and Hang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 中敏所善李款，字言源。

translations.literal: Li Kuan, whom Zhongmin befriended, had courtesy name Yanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuan, whom Zhongmin befriended, was styled Yanyuan.

sentences.zh: 長慶初第進士，爲侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he passed the jinshi examination and became Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing he passed the jinshi examination and became Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 注自邠寧入朝，款伏閣劾奏：「注內通敕使，外結朝臣，往來兩地，卜射賕謝。」

translations.literal: When Zhu entered court from Binning, Kuan prostrated himself at the gate and impeached: "Zhu communicates inward with edict envoys and outward binds court officials, traveling between both places, divining and offering bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu entered court from Binning, Kuan prostrated himself at the gate and impeached him: "Zhu communicates with edict envoys within and binds court officials without, traveling between both and offering bribes.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 後浸用事，款被斥去。

translations.literal: Later Zhu gradually wielded power and Kuan was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu gradually wielded power and Kuan was driven out.

sentences.zh: 注死，由倉部員外郎累遷江西觀察使。

translations.literal: After Zhu's death, from Vice Director of the Granary Bureau he was repeatedly promoted to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu's death he rose from Vice Director of the Granary Bureau to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 終澶王傅。

translations.literal: He ended as Tutor of the Prince of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Tutor of the Prince of Chan.

sentences.zh: 李甘李甘，字和鼎。

translations.literal: Li Gan, courtesy name Heding.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, styled Heding.

sentences.zh: 長慶末，第進士，舉賢良方正異等。

translations.literal: At the end of Changqing he passed the jinshi examination and was nominated for the Worthy and Upright special examination in the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changqing he passed the jinshi examination and ranked top in the Worthy and Upright special examination.

sentences.zh: 累擢侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 鄭注侍講禁中，求宰相，朝廷嘩言將用之，甘顯倡曰：「宰相代天治物者，當先德望，後文藝。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu lectured within the forbidden precincts and sought the chief ministership; the court clamored that he would be used; Gan openly led saying: "The chief minister who governs things for Heaven should put virtue and reputation first, literary accomplishment second.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu lectured in the inner palace and sought the chief ministership; the court buzzed that he would be appointed; Gan openly declared: "The chief minister who governs for Heaven should put virtue first and literary talent second.

sentences.zh: 注何人，欲得宰相？

translations.literal: What sort of man is Zhu to seek the chief ministership?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man is Zhu to seek the chief ministership?

sentences.zh: 白麻出，我必壞之。」

translations.literal: When the white hemp edict comes out, I will surely destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict comes out, I will tear it up.

sentences.zh: 既而麻出，乃以趙儋爲鄜坊節度使，甘坐輕肆，貶封州司馬。

translations.literal: When the edict came out it appointed Zhao Dan as Bian-Fang Military Commissioner; Gan was punished for levity and demoted to military administrator of Feng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came out it appointed Zhao Dan as Bian-Fang Military Commissioner; Gan was punished for levity and demoted to military administrator of Feng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而李訓內亦惡注，由是注卒不相。

translations.literal: Yet Li Xun inwardly also hated Zhu; thus Zhu ultimately did not become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun also hated Zhu inwardly; thus Zhu never became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 甘終於貶。

translations.literal: Gan ended in demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Gan died in exile.

sentences.zh: 始，河南人楊牢，字松年，有至行。

translations.literal: Initially Yang Lao of Henan, courtesy name Songnian, had supreme conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lao of Henan, styled Songnian, was a man of supreme filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 甘方未顯，以書薦於尹曰：「執事之部孝童楊牢，父茂卿，從田氏府，趙軍反，殺田氏，茂卿死。

translations.literal: When Gan was not yet prominent he recommended in a letter to the intendant: "The filial youth Yang Lao in your jurisdiction—his father Maoqing followed the Tian household; when Zhao's army rebelled they killed the Tian clan and Maoqing died.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gan was prominent he wrote the intendant recommending: "The filial youth Yang Lao in your jurisdiction—his father Maoqing served the Tian household; when Zhao's army rebelled they killed the Tian clan and Maoqing died.

sentences.zh: 牢之兄蜀，三往索父喪，慮死不果至。

translations.literal: Lao's elder brother Shu went three times to claim their father's body but feared death and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Lao's elder brother Shu went three times to claim their father's body but feared death and failed.

sentences.zh: 牢自洛陽走常山二千里，號伏叛壘，委發羸骸，有可憐狀，讎意感解，以尸還之。

translations.literal: Lao ran two thousand li from Luoyang to Changshan, wailing and prostrate before the rebel camp, with disheveled hair and emaciated frame in pitiable state; the enemy's intent was moved and released, returning the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Lao ran two thousand li from Luoyang to Changshan, wailing and prostrate before the rebel camp, disheveled and emaciated in pitiable state; the enemy was moved and returned the corpse.

sentences.zh: 單縗冬月，往來太行間，凍膚皸瘃，銜哀雨血。

translations.literal: In unlined hemp mourning garb in winter months he traveled between the Taihang ranges, skin frost-cracked and chilblained, bearing grief like rain of blood.
translations.idiomatic: In unlined hemp mourning garb in winter he traveled the Taihang ranges, skin frost-cracked, grief like blood rain.

sentences.zh: 行路稠人爲牢泣，歸責其子，以牢勉之。

translations.literal: Crowds on the road wept for Lao; returning home they reproached their sons and used Lao to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds on the road wept for Lao; returning home they reproached their sons and held Lao up as example.

sentences.zh: 牢爲兒踐操如此，未聞執事門唁而書顯之，豈樹風扶教意耶？

translations.literal: Lao as a youth practiced conduct such as this; I have not heard that Your Excellency's gate sent condolences or displayed it in writing—is this the intent of establishing custom and supporting instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Lao showed such conduct as a youth; I have not heard that Your Excellency sent condolences or honored him in writing—is this how custom and instruction are supported?

sentences.zh: 且鄕人能嚙疽刳昚，急親之病，皆一時決耳，猶蒙表其閭，脫之徭，上有大禮則差問以粟帛。

translations.literal: Moreover villagers who bite abscesses or cut flesh for parents' urgent illness—all momentary decisions—still receive commendation of their hamlet, exemption from corvée, and when the sovereign performs great rites, inquiry with grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers who bite abscesses or cut flesh for parents' illness—all momentary acts—still receive hamlet commendation, corvée exemption, and imperial gifts at great rites.

sentences.zh: 今河北驕叛，萬師不能攘，而牢徙步請尸仇手，與夫含腐忍瘡者孰多？

translations.literal: Now Hebei is arrogant and rebellious; ten thousand troops cannot suppress it—yet Lao walked on foot to claim a corpse from the enemy's hand; compared with those who hold rotten flesh and endure sores, which is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Hebei rebels defy ten thousand troops—yet Lao walked on foot to claim his father's corpse from the enemy; compared with those who merely endure sores for parents, which is greater?

sentences.zh: 牢絶乳即能詩，洛陽兒曹壯於牢者皆出其下。

translations.literal: Lao could compose poetry as soon as he was weaned; lads in Luoyang stronger than Lao were all beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Lao could compose poetry as soon as he was weaned; boys in Luoyang stronger than he were all his inferiors.

sentences.zh: 聞牢之贖喪，潞帥償其費，其葬也，滑帥賻之財，斯執事之事，他人既篡之矣。

translations.literal: I hear that for Lao's redeeming the funeral the Lu commander repaid his costs; for the burial the Hua commander gave funeral gifts—these were Your Excellency's affairs, yet others have usurped them.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Lu commander repaid Lao's funeral costs and the Hua commander gave burial gifts—these were Your Excellency's affairs, yet others have usurped them.

sentences.zh: 即有稱牢於上者，執事能無恨其後乎？」

translations.literal: If someone praises Lao to the sovereign, can Your Excellency not resent being left behind?
translations.idiomatic: If someone praises Lao to the throne, will Your Excellency not resent being left behind?

sentences.zh: 其激卬自任類此。

translations.literal: His passionate self-assurance was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His passionate self-assurance was like this.

sentences.zh: 牢後亦擢進士第。

translations.literal: Lao later also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Lao later also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：夫以下摩上，士所甚患，然取名最多，故上失德則與下爭名，而後有誅夷斥竄事。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: For inferiors to remonstrate upward is what gentlemen greatly dread, yet it wins the most fame; thus when superiors lose virtue they contend with inferiors for fame, and afterward come execution, exile, and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: Remonstrance from below is what gentlemen dread, yet it wins the most fame; when superiors lose virtue they contend with inferiors for reputation, and execution and exile follow.

sentences.zh: 然或依古肆言，高而難從，以邀主賈直者，逆之似傷道，行之不切時，此言事常弊也。

translations.literal: Yet some rely on antiquity and speak freely, lofty and hard to follow, inviting the sovereign to buy bluntness—opposing this seems to harm the Way, enacting it does not suit the times; this is the common fault of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some cite antiquity and speak loftily, hard to follow, inviting the sovereign to reward bluntness—opposing this seems to harm the Way, enacting it suits not the times; this is remonstrance's common fault.

sentences.zh: 若廷珪數子，優游彌縫，皆中時病，非所謂賈直自榮者也。

translations.literal: Men like Tinggui and several others, easy and mending, all hit the ailments of the age—they are not what is called selling bluntness for self-glory.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Tinggui and his fellows, measured and mending, all hit the ailments of the age—they did not sell bluntness for self-glory.

sentences.zh: 至渤爭晏朝，潾諫方士，甘斥鄭注不可作宰相，排寵救危，不得不爾，賢哉！

translations.literal: As for Bo contending over delayed court, Lin remonstrating against alchemists, Gan denouncing Zheng Zhu as unfit for chief minister—rejecting favor and saving peril, they could not do otherwise—how worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Bo contending over delayed court, Lin remonstrating against alchemists, Gan denouncing Zheng Zhu as unfit for chief minister—rejecting favor and saving peril, they could not do otherwise—how worthy!
